title: The first thing you should do on Googlebook is fix the trackpad
snippet: If you are an early Googlebook buyer, you should know that one of the first changes you should make on one of these new machines is to adjust the trackpad speed, because it’s a bit frustrating out of the box. more…
fullText:
If you are an early Googlebook buyer, you should know that one of the first changes you should make on one of these new machines is to adjust the trackpad speed, because it’s a bit frustrating out of the box.

Every Googlebook in this initial wave comes with a haptic trackpad, but they also seem to have a slight headache out of the box.

The cursor is incredibly slow.

“Touchpad accleration” on Googlebook, at least by default, is considerably slower than other platforms such as Windows and macOS. It’s something that we’ve all noticed here on the 9to5Google team as we’ve started using Googlebook machines this week across multiple models. It’s far from unusable, but it’s very jarring compared to any other laptop you might go buy at the store today. 

	

Luckily, it can be fixed fairly easily. Go to Settings > Device & accessories > Touchpad > Cursor speed  and you’ll be able to adjust the setting to your preferences. For me, that meant maxing it out to get something more akin to my other machines. 

You’ll have to complete inital setup before you can adjust this setting.

title: Full Disk Access on Mac: Here’s what Apple must, and must not, do
snippet: We’ve seen a number of examples of why giving Meta’s Muse app full disk access to your Mac is a very bad idea, and yet another major privacy issue has recently been discovered. It’s now been found that Muse analyzes your communication with everyone in your life on an hourly basis. Apple is rightly concerned about the development, and in a blog post says that it will be introducing additional controls around the Full Disk Access feature that’s been enabling the problems … more…
fullText:
We’ve seen a number of examples of why giving Meta’s Muse app full disk access to your Mac is a very bad idea, and yet another major privacy issue has recently been discovered. It’s now been found that Muse analyzes your communication with everyone in your life on an hourly basis.

Apple is rightly concerned about the development, and in a blog post says that it will be introducing additional controls around the Full Disk Access feature that’s been enabling the problems … 

Meta recently launched its Muse Personal AI Agent for iPhone and Mac. Despite the obvious inadvisability of giving a Meta app unfettered access to everything on your Apple devices, the app quickly jumped to the top of the App Store.

Predictably, it wasn’t long before things started to go horribly wrong. Things haven’t gotten any better since then, with Wired reporting that security researcher Karan Joshi found Meta had instructed Muse to extract all of the information needed to construct a complete map of all of your relationships.

One of Muse’s instructions appears to be the ability for it to create “a page for every person in the user’s life.” This hourly process involves compiling data on family, partners, friends, colleagues, “collaborators,” and people you “follow,” the instructions say […]

“Where they live, what they do, the threads that recur (the apartment move, the shared savings goal),” the instructions say. They add, too, that the model could record the “dates that matter,” such as birthdays or anniversaries. A person’s history could include backstory like “the trip in March, the argument that got resolved, the milestone last week.”

Apple tightening use of Full Disk Access

You would think a permission prompt to give an app “full disk access” to your Mac would be self-explanatory, but it appears not. Even tech-savvy people have been granting this access-all-areas pass to their machines without appreciating just how dangerous a step it is.

Apple says the feature was intended for backup apps, but developers are now using it for many more things, including AI agents. The company has said it intends to “introduce additional controls” to ensure users fully understand what they are doing if they grant this permission.

Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.

Here’s what Apple must – and must not – do

Apple says it is “critical” to take this step, and I fully agree. When it’s become clear that the existing permission request doesn’t fully communicate the gravity of granting it, it’s essential that Apple ensure users genuinely understand what it is they are allowing.

What I’d like to see is far more explicit text advising people against doing it unless they are certain they understand the consequences. Something along the lines:

This app is requesting full disk access to your Mac, aka an access-all-areas pass to your data. Apple intended this feature to be used only by backup apps. If you grant permission, this app will be able to read all of your personal data, including all of your messages with other people. Giving permission is extremely dangerous and should never be done unless you are completely confident that you understand what the app will do with your data and that you have complete trust in the developer. Your default response to this permission request should be No.

Essentially, there is no wording that would be too strong. I’d also be fine with a one-off confirmation of the apps already given this permission.

	

However, what Apple absolutely must not do is to make the mistake it made with macOS Sequoia over screen recording. Sure, this is also incredibly dangerous and very strong warnings are appropriate, but what Apple did then was to force us all to confirm these permissions on a weekly basis, as well as after every restart. 

This was widely condemned as turning macOS into Microsoft Vista and imposing “a subscription you didn’t buy and can’t cancel.” In my view, Apple already goes too far in this direction with its occasional requests for repeated permission confirmations on iPhone. I gave Citymapper permission to access my location so that it can continue to provide directions in the background, for example, and no, Apple, I really don’t need you to check I still want this.

Yes, issue the strongest of warnings against granting full disk access, but if someone chooses to do so, then macOS must accept their decision. No forced confirmations, weekly or otherwise, thank you.

Apple is working on a new ecosystem of smart home devices via a partnership with LG, Bloomberg has reported.

title: Spotify expands audiobooks to over 180 markets
snippet: Spotify will make 350,000 titles available in over 120 languages for this expansion.
fullText:
Spotify announced on Wednesday that it’s expanding audiobook access to over 180 markets worldwide, including regions across Europe, the Americas, the Caribbean, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. The rollout is starting today and will continue over the coming months. With this move, more than 750 million users will be able to access audiobooks, allowing Spotify to better compete with both music streaming providers and audiobook apps like Audible.

Before this, audiobooks were available primarily in English-speaking markets like the U.S., U.K., Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand, as well as in Germany. 

The audio platform said it has more than 350,000 titles for its new markets and has increased its collection to include over 120 languages. With its launch in Spain, users in the country will have access to over 45,000 titles in Spanish. 

Spotify is working with more than 300 publishers worldwide, including Planeta and Mondadori, to increase the number of titles available in different markets.

With a Premium subscription, users can listen to 12 hours of audiobooks in eligible countries such as Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, Poland, Chile, Norway, and Peru. People across the world can also purchase an Audiobook+ stand-alone subscription to get access to titles with a 15-hour allowance. Alternatively, users can buy individual titles directly.

Spotify is also adding an Audiobook+ add-on for student plans in select regions in November. The company said that since its launch last year, Audiobook+ has gained over 1 million subscribers and has fetched over 100 million in annual recurring revenue for the platform.  

In February, the company launched a “Page Match” feature, which lets users scan a page of a physical book and find the corresponding point in the audiobook to listen to. Since the launch, 1 million people have been using the feature monthly, the company noted. 

Spotify said that over the last year, monthly listeners of audiobooks grew by 40% and listening hours increased by 30%.

This year, the company introduced Audiobook Charts to let people discover popular titles. It also launched an AI-powered tool for authors to turn their books into audiobooks using models from ElevenLabs. Plus, Spotify started experimenting with physical sales of books through its audiobook platform in select markets like the U.S. and the U.K.

title: Mistral’s New ‘Le Chonk’ AI Model Is Big, Open and Built for Agents
snippet: Mistral Large 4 is a state-of-the-art model for cyberdefense, manufacturing, finance-related tasks and multimodal use.
fullText:
New AI models are coming, and they don’t stop coming. 

On the heels of the recent rollout of Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, Mistral AI is launching a new flagship model, Mistral Large 4, with a public preview available on Tuesday.

A French company known for its open-source and open-weight LLMs, Mistral AI reports that the Large 4 model “ranks among the best open-weight models of the world” on aggregated metrics and also outperforms European and US models, while also catching up to Chinese competitors, who have been dominating the open-weight sector. 

			

More from CNET

I talked with Mistral Chief Scientist Guillaume Lample and VP of Science Pierre Stock about the new model – affectionately known as “le Chonk” – its specialized capabilities and extreme compute efficiency. Here’s what to know. 

Key capabilities of Mistral Large 4

Lample and Stock said that Mistral Large 4 was built to process both text and images, closing performance gaps from previous Mistral models. Specifically, Large 4 touts more advanced cybersecurity and agentic capabilities, as well as a better ability to handle manufacturing- and finance-related tasks.

Cybersecurity

Mistral Large 4 was designed to excel at defensive cybersecurity tasks, including log inspection, code auditing and checking for newly published exploits or vulnerabilities. Beyond defensive measures, Mistral says the new model offers offensive cybersecurity measures to identify and address weaknesses. 

Agentic AI

“Really, the core competency we’re looking at for ML4 is agentic capabilities,” said Stock. 

Mistral Large 4 was built with a focus on agentic performance for planning, research or handling complex enterprise tasks that would take human experts hours or days to complete. The Mistral AI team said the model reaches “state-of-the-art” performance on critical agentic benchmarks like SWE-bench and Terminal Bench – evaluation frameworks for testing how well agents handle complex tasks – for tasks like coding, analyzing and pulling requests. 

Geospatial and grounding capabilities

The Mistral team says the model outperforms competitors in aerial and satellite imagery analysis, with the capacity to identify visual patterns and objects on maps, such as forest fires. 

“On grounding capabilities, it outperforms all existing models, including the closed ones,” the press release for the model says. “These are critical as cyberattacks get faster and cheaper, companies write more code than ever and the world needs more chips to keep up with AI demand.”

Grounding is a technique used in AI development to try to eliminate hallucinations – when the LLM generates inaccurate information – by anchoring the AI’s outputs in external resources, like documents and databases, rather than just the materials it was trained on internally. Grounding also helps keep data and information fresh while providing context for the AI’s responses. 

Mistral says the new model was also trained on more than 160 languages, including every official language of the European Union, as well as Latin and non-Latin languages, to answer prompts natively. 

Mistral will roll out ML4 on Oct. 27. Until then, the model is available for a public preview period, allowing the Mistral team to further assess it with feedback from developers, cybersecurity experts and state officials. The team will also use this period for additional reinforcement learning and fine-tuning. You can try the preview API here.

Over 45,000 organizations trust Mosyle to make millions of Apple devices work ready with no effort and at an affordable cost. Request your EXTENDED TRIAL today and understand why Mosyle is everything you need to work with Apple.

MacPaw spent nearly two decades building consumer software for Mac users. CleanMyMac is one of the Mac utilities on the market, and it’s my go-to when I need to free up hard drive space, uninstall apps, etc. The company is making a different kind of bet with Leebry, a Work AI platform aimed at helping IT teams.

About Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers has been an Apple IT admin since 2009. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, a mobile device management system, enterprise grade WiFi, 1000s of Macs, and 1000s of iPads, Bradley will highlight ways in which Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train users, share stories from the trenches of IT management, and ways Apple could improve its products for IT departments.

The AI trust numbers

MacPaw’s 2026 AI at Work report is where you see the issue IT faces, as they found that 90% of companies deploy AI without thoroughly auditing their internal knowledge base first. That means that internal AI tools are answering employee questions based on whatever it can find, including old product docs, outdated policies, and random Reddit discussion forums.

In this survey, MacPaw found that 6 in 10 IT leaders see a real disconnect between what their C-Suite expects from AI tools (thanks to LinkedIn feeds) and what their teams can safely and accurately deliver. That gap is where most AI disappointment lives, and it’s the problem Leebry is attempting to solve for IT teams.

What Leebry actually does

Leebry began as an internal MacPaw hackathon project in 2025. The problem it was solving was employees repeatedly asking the same questions internally, even when the answers already existed somewhere in the company’s documentation, intranets, Slack threads, etc. MacPaw built a Slack bot to surface those answers and point employees to the exact source. Within a few months, it was resolving 30% of MacPaw’s own level 1 IT tickets, so that became the foundation for what they’re launching today with Leebry.

The platform automates level 1 support tickets, handles access provisioning and removal as employees join, move roles, or leave, and answers employee questions across the tools they already use. Every Leebry response links back to its source, so employees can verify the answer rather than just trust it (and prove it), and can flag stale or outdated information that could affect accuracy. That last part is the direct product response to the 90% knowledge audit problem from their own research.

One detail worth calling out for security-conscious IT folks: Leebry is permission-aware, meaning it authenticates each user and surfaces only the information they are permitted to see. That matters more than it sounds as a lot of AI tools draw on a shared knowledge pool and let users surface things they shouldn’t access. Leebry also ships with an MCP server that exposes the device management control plane to AI agents, with admin-set guardrails on every action, so teams can delegate repetitive work to agents without giving up control over what those agents can actually do.

For IT orgs that work extensively with Apple, the access provisioning aspect is interesting. Automating access changes as people move within the organization can be a huge pain point for SMBs without a dedicated IAM team. Most of the time, it’s manual, it’s slow, and departing employees end up with access that should have been revoked days earlier. I’ve run into this myself quite a bit.

“Businesses don’t need another tool to check, they need work taken off their plate, without sacrificing oversight or control,” said Dan Jaenicke, Director of B2B Product Development at MacPaw.

Wrap up

The fair question here is why an IT team should trust a consumer Mac software company to build enterprise tooling. I think the answer is actually in the product’s origin story. MacPaw built Leebry to solve their own internal IT problem first, which is a better foundation than most enterprise software gets. It wasn’t built to make money. It was built to solve a customer (even internal) problem, so it’ll work well for other teams. The reality is all orgs have docs spread out across team chat, file sharing, intranets, etc and we’re all guilty of asking for someone else to find it for us.

Leebry aims to make it easy for IT to solve the same questions folks ask over and over again.

title: Google AI Edge Foresight for Mac turns scribbles into full notes using offline recordings
snippet: Google today announced its new EmbeddingGemma 2 model that can be used to “organize, search, and connect information directly on consumer hardware.” To show off its potential, Google created an AI Edge Foresight Mac app for “intelligent notetaking.” more…
fullText:
Google today announced its new EmbeddingGemma 2 model that can be used to “organize, search, and connect information directly on consumer hardware.” To show off its potential, Google created an AI Edge Foresight Mac app for “intelligent notetaking.”

EmbeddingGemma 2 “can help find a specific video clip from a voice memo, or search through hours of audio recordings based on a text query, all processed by a single, natively multimodal model.”

The 740 million parameter model is built on the Gemma 4 architecture and available with an Apache 2.0 license. This is meant to run locally “within tight resource constraints”:

With quantization, on a Google Pixel 11 Pro, EmbeddingGemma 2 requires as little as ~191MB active RAM for text-only weights and ~567MB for the full multimodal model.

To showcase, there are demos in Google AI Edge Gallery on Android and iOS. The bigger showcase is a new Mac app called Google AI Edge Foresight.

	

During video or in-person meetings, this notetaking app listens in the background so that you can just “scribble shorthand bullets for things you want to remember.”

The app, leveraging EmbeddingGemma 2, “enriches [that shorthand] into polished notes using the meeting transcript instantly.” The transcript and audio are processed entirely on your device rather than the cloud.

Another capability lets you “point Google AI Edge Foresight to your project folders, reference materials, diagrams, and calendar.” Supporting local files and Google Drive, this in turn lets you ask the app questions and quickly get back information.

It automatically understands your work without needing to manually organize your files, to ensure critical information is ready whenever you need it.

The chat feature offers “conversational retrieval and summary with your personal knowledge.” There’s also a Live Assistance capability that will “listen and automatically answer questions.”

You can download Google AI Edge Foresight here. This joins Google’s two other Mac apps in the family: AI Edge Gallery and AI Edge Eloquent (offline transcription).

title: Pixel 10a gets a $100 price hike, now starting at $599

fullText:
Google has quietly raised the price of its mid-range Pixel 10a by $100, giving the device a starting price of $599.

In our review of Pixel 10a, we called the device a “well-rounded experience” for its $499 price, but a $100 jump certainly makes that a tougher conversation, especially considering Google’s mid-ranger is at this point using a two-generation-old chipset in its Tensor G4. title: The Pixel 3a might be the most important Google smartphone to date
snippet: Google Pixel was designed to be a premium smartphone effort, but that all changed in 2019 with the debut of the Pixel 3a. The budget-conscious launch went on to be a turning point for the Pixel’s history and, looking back, it might just be the single most important Google smartphone ever. more…
fullText:
Google Pixel was designed to be a premium smartphone effort, but that all changed in 2019 with the debut of the Pixel 3a. The budget-conscious launch went on to be a turning point for the Pixel’s history and, looking back, it might just be the single most important Google smartphone ever.

Looking back over the past decade of Pixel smartphones, I’m not sure you can point at any one device and say it was more important than the Pixel 3a. The original Pixel set the foundation, of course, and Pixel 6 launched Google’s efforts into a new era, but Pixel 3a gave Google a taste of what it was always after – market success.

The Pixel 3a almost immediately shot up to the top of best-seller lists, massively propelled Google’s US smartphone sales, and was the driving force behind setting Google’s first big shipment records. That success ultimately led to several Pixel A-series successors that have similarly resonated in the market. These more affordable devices just nail the fundamentals at a price that’s hard to beat, especially considering the cost of a Pixel 10a is only $100 more (annnnnnd now it’s $200) than the Pixel 3a originally started at.

Google is finding at least some success in the flagship market nowadays. Pixel phones are very much hitting their stride in 2026 not only in terms of design and functionality, but also in the market as a whole. I’d very much argue, though, that the Pixel 3a was the lifejacket that kept this project going. The failure of the Pixel 4 left scars on Google’s smartphone efforts, but the Pixel 3a’s resounding success was surely a huge deciding factor on what would come next.

	
	

And, in 2026, I think this phone holds up remarkably well from a hardware perspective. There are modern budget phones that cost just as much as the Pixel 3a did when it came out that feel a lot worse than this one. The Pixel 3a is long dead at this point with software support having ended in 2022, but its legacy lives on.

fullText:
The current beta of iOS 27.2 includes a Siri AI “suggested actions” feature in the Messages app that some will consider useful and others find annoying. 

A developer who has found a number of unannounced features has discovered that Apple is seeking to keep everyone happy with a new set of options …

Suggested Actions in Messages

Suggested Actions were present in the initial iOS 27 beta, but Apple later pulled the feature after complaints that some of the suggestions were rather random. It subsequently returned in the beta of iOS 27.2. Here’s how Apple describes it:

Messages offers one-tap suggestions based on the context of users’ conversations, making it easier than ever to get things done, such as creating a reminder or a note. For example, if someone asks for photos, Messages can also help users find the right ones, recognizing keywords, locations, and people in their library to find the best options.

In the first example shown above, a group message chat contains a request for some shopping and to bring something left behind. The Messages app offers one-tap options to Add to Reminders and Add to Notes. In the second example, someone asks for specific photos to be shared, and the Messages app offers a button which leads directly to a search for matching photos.

Two ways to hide unwanted suggestions

Leaker pdfu found new controls in iOS 27.2 beta 3 to selectively toggle off unwanted suggestions.

These allow suggestions to be toggled off by category, or you can let Siri AI monitor which ones you do and don’t use, and have it automatically hide the categories you haven’t used in the last 30 days.

These options aren’t yet live in the beta, but we can likely expect to see them soon.

9to5Mac’s Take

I’m certainly one of those who found many of them more annoying than useful, while I know others who are big fans, so this change ought to keep everyone happy.

title: OpenAI details new text watermarking system for ChatGPT, Codex, and the API
snippet: OpenAI today announced how it will comply with the EU AI Act, which requires providers of generative AI systems to mark AI-generated text in a way that makes it identifiable. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
OpenAI today announced how it will comply with the EU AI Act, which requires providers of generative AI systems to mark AI-generated text in a way that makes it identifiable. Here are the details.

A bit of context

A few months ago, Anthropic sparked controversy when it announced that, to comply with the EU AI Act, Claude would start watermarking text by slightly adjusting its word choice.

In a nutshell, every so often, Claude chooses between words that would work equally well based on a hidden pattern, which Anthropic says has no practical impact on the meaning, quality, or readability of its responses.

Anthropic also developed a detector that can look for that pattern in a piece of text, and can tell whether it likely came from Claude.

The detector can’t be used to determine whether text came from OpenAI or any other competitor, since Claude’s watermark is generated using a secret key specific to Anthropic’s system.

At the height of the controversy, Anthropic stressed that Claude would not be alone, noting that several other major AI providers were also implementing marking systems to comply with the EU’s requirements.

Today, OpenAI announced its own solution, which relies on a similar approach, albeit with a much more limited rollout and scope.

OpenAI’s text watermarking system

According to OpenAI, “API customers globally will be able to opt in to text watermarking for select models” starting today, while the company “will add an invisible watermark to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text output in the European Union” in the coming weeks.

This means that in the API, text watermarking will remain off by default for now, while in ChatGPT and Codex, it will initially be limited to eligible users only in the European Union.

OpenAI also opened applications for access to its text watermark detector, which will initially be limited to approved researchers and expert organizations as the company works to evaluate and improve the technology.

And speaking of accuracy, OpenAI is very clear that the detection technology still has significant limitations, as it can produce both false negatives and false positives, particularly with shorter texts or content in specific domains, “such as mathematics, where there is less flexibility in word choice.”

Here’s OpenAI on textGrain, which is its text watermarking technology:

Our text watermarking technology, textGrain, adds an invisible statistical signal to the model’s word choices. Our detector looks for that signal to assess whether a passage contains an OpenAI watermark. More details about how textGrain works can be found in our technical report⁠, which will be updated with additional details in the coming weeks. We also plan to make the technology available in open source so that others can build on it.

The company also noted that, in addition to being harder to detect in shorter passages, the watermark can be significantly weakened by editing:

In an evaluation of 400-token passages, replacing 10% of words with synonyms reduced detection from about 92% to 66%. Replacing 25% of words reduced it to 17%.

Interestingly, OpenAI’s comparison of watermarked and unwatermarked text showed that watermarked outputs actually scored slightly higher on several benchmarks, despite the company saying it found no meaningful difference in overall performance.

OpenAI also stressed that, in addition to the false positive and false negative shortcomings, a watermark “does not measure human contribution,” “does not establish ownership or responsibility,” “does not identify the user,” and “does not verify accuracy.”

OpenAI added that “the absence of a detected watermark does not prove human authorship” either.

Finally, the company said it expects to revisit its approach as the technology, standards, and evidence evolve, while continuing to study how well watermarks survive editing and translation and whether they can more meaningfully distinguish AI assistance from AI authorship.

title: Nvidia Shield TV Pro is now $299 – a $100 price hike seven years after the Android TV box launched
snippet: The Nvidia Shield TV is an iconic piece of Android hardware but it also hasn’t seen a refresh in the better part of a decade. But, because of the increasingly depressing state of the entire tech industry, Nvidia Shield TV Pro is getting a $100 price hike to $299, seven years after it first launched. more…
fullText:
The Nvidia Shield TV is an iconic piece of Android hardware but it also hasn’t seen a refresh in the better part of a decade. But, because of the increasingly depressing state of the entire tech industry, Nvidia Shield TV Pro is getting a $100 price hike to $299, seven years after it first launched.

Nvidia Shield TV Pro made its debut in October 2019 and, to this day, remains one of the most capable Android TV streamers on the market. While certain aspects haven’t aged perfectly, such as a lack of AV1 support and others, it remains unmatched in other places.

That’s a big part of the reason that, even so many years after it launched, Nvidia continues to produce the Shield TV.

But the $199 price point is gone. Effective today, Nvidia Shield TV Pro now costs $299.99. Nvidia attributed the price hike to the fact that “the cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry.” Alongside the change in price, Nvidia has also ended production of the base Shield TV that was also introduced in 2019. The “tube” Shield has been out of stock for months at this point, but Shield TV Pro was just restocked at Best Buy.

	

Shield TV Pro at Best Buy

Early this year, Nvidia said that it would continue software support for the Shield TV for the forseeable future. 

Shield isn’t the only streamer going up in price as a result of RAMageddon. Google TV Streamer saw a price hike to $149 recently, while other devices including Apple TV 4K and various Roku streamers also saw price hikes earlier this year. 

AI is just great, right?

Amazon doesn't specify how many turns are needed but claims just "a few times" can generate enough power to unlock the door so you can gain access to your home and fully recharge the lock's battery. The Ring Smart Lock is expected to be available in the US sometime in ea … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

Amazon announced its first smart lock that eliminates the need for a physical backup key should its rechargeable battery die while you’re away from home. While other smart locks lean on hidden USB ports or metal contacts for connecting a 9-volt battery to replenish a dead battery, the new Ring Smart Lock incorporates a more convenient charger right into its thumb-turn dial. Amazon doesn’t specify how many turns are needed but claims just “a few times” can generate enough power to unlock the door so you can gain access to your home and fully recharge the lock’s battery.

The Ring Smart Lock is expected to be available in the US sometime in early 2027 (pending FCC approval) and will be offered in black, silver, and brass finishes for $249. Unlocking options include a fingerprint reader and a backlit touchscreen keypad with the option to register multiple users and schedule when they have access to your home. This includes setting up temporary access codes that automatically expire after a set amount of time. The Ring Smart Lock can also be opened, locked, and monitored using the Ring mobile app or controlled using voice commands through Alexa-compatible devices like Echo smart speakers.

Installation doesn’t require any wiring since the Smart Lock uses Ring’s replaceable Quick Release Ultra Battery Pack, and instead of relying on your home’s Wi-Fi, the lock wirelessly connects to other devices using Amazon’s low-power, low-bandwidth, long-range Sidewalk network. Assuming you live somewhere with adequate Sidewalk coverage, you won’t have to worry about Wi-Fi outages preventing you from granting remote access or getting alerts about who’s just entered your home.

The Ring Smart Lock doesn’t include a camera, so you’ll need to pair it with a smart doorbell to see who’s accessing your home or one of five new Ring security cameras expanding Amazon’s collection of “Retinal Vision 4K” devices that first debuted a year ago. Starting today, you can preorder the new $149.99 Outdoor Cam 4K Plus that’s available in battery, wired, solar, and PoE versions, the $199.99 Spotlight Cam 4K Plus featuring a 550-lumen deterrent light, and the $219.99 Floodlight Cam 4K Plus that can illuminate large spaces while offering 24/7 recording with smart subject detection. But you won’t have to wait for the first indoor Ring camera with Retinal 4K. The $99.99 Indoor Cam 4K is available for purchase today and features a 115-degree field of view with a shutter that physically blocks the camera when privacy is needed.

Alongside all the new 4K options, Amazon is also introducing a new entry-level 2K indoor camera that’s available starting today for $69.99. The Ring Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K uses “computer vision–based motion detection” to track subjects like pets moving around a room. The camera can rotate a full 360 degrees while tilting 175 degrees to keep subjects in frame, and like Ring’s new 4K indoor camera, the 2K version incorporates a physical privacy shutter that disables both the camera and its microphone when it’s closed.

title: Google Home update rolling out with better ‘Find My Phone’ voice commands, smart home improvements
snippet: A new Google Home update has arrived with various improvements including better support for the “Find My Phone” voice command on Gemini speakers. more…
fullText:
A new Google Home update has arrived with various improvements including better support for the “Find My Phone” voice command on Gemini speakers.

In the Gemini for Home early access branch, Google says that users can expect “quality and reliability improvements” for the “Hey Google, find my phone” command that’s been around for years. It’s unclear exactly what’s changing, but this is a very useful voice command, so any upgrades will be welcome.

Improved Find My Phone reliability: Rolled out quality and reliability improvements to this fan-favorite feature when you ask Gemini to help locate your phone.

Other Gemini voice improvements in this latest update include filtering out background noise and voices, further speed/latency improvements, better support for multilingual households, and improved reliability to custom commands within Routines/automations.

In the Google Home app itself, there are quite a few updates to smart home functionality. This includes turning off lights when the brightness slider is dragged down to zero, improving camera and doorbell tiles, reducing Matter switches being incorrectly shown as offline, and improving setup for Nest devices.

	

Device Controller Enhancements

Accurate smart light shutoff: We’ve resolved an issue where sliding brightness down to 0% on single lights or group dimmers left bulbs powered on at minimum illumination instead of turning them off completely. Lowering your brightness to 0% now sends a definitive power-off command, preventing wasted energy and unexpected ambient glow.

Clearer online camera and doorbell tiles: Online cameras and doorbells now show as filled icons and accented tile colors at a glance, helping you instantly distinguish active cameras from idle ones.

Accurate offline switch status: We’ve resolved an issue where Matter switches failed to show their offline status or respond to taps on the All Devices tab, ensuring tiles properly render greyed out when disconnected.

Reliable Favorites tile gestures: We’ve resolved issues where long-pressing tiles in the Favorites tab failed to open device controllers or routine editors.

Smarter window covering detection: We’ve corrected device type resolution so awnings and curtains map accurately instead of defaulting all open-and-close window coverings to blinds.

Setup Improvements

Smoother smart device setup: We’ve delivered end-to-end reliability improvements when setting up Nest devices across iOS and Android. This includes under-the-hood fixes for Bluetooth connections and Wi-Fi pairing to eliminate common dropouts and stalls during the initial setup process.

Faster, standalone setup: When adding a new device to your home, the Google Home app can now securely cache network credentials on your mobile device, and reuse them for your next device.

There’s also a new preview option for Nest Doorbell ringtones.

The app update is rolling out now on Android, v4.31.27.1, while the Gemini updates are happening behind the scenes for those in early access.

title: Oracle Health Hack Exposes Data of Nearly 20M People
snippet: Patient names, Social Security numbers, doctors and diagnoses might have been breached in the cyberattack.
fullText:
A cyberattack against Oracle Health last year exposed the personal data of almost 20 million people, the Texas attorney general’s office said in a report, according to Bloomberg.

The personal information taken by the attacker included Social Security numbers, addresses and medical information, Oracle disclosed to investigators. The cybersecurity breach happened after Jan. 22, 2025, and Oracle alerted some customers about it in March of that year, Bloomberg reported. 

Oracle Health is a division of Oracle, which acquired healthcare technology company Cerner for $28.3 billion in June 2022.

			

More from CNET

Oracle told its customers that attackers had targeted older Cerner servers before the data stored on them could be migrated to Oracle’s cloud storage service, Bloomberg said. The hacker compromised customer credentials and used them to access two Cerner servers and then copied patient data from those servers, according to UK cybersecurity firm CyPro.

Neither Oracle nor the Texas attorney general specified which hospitals, clinics or other healthcare providers were affected by the data theft.

CNET reached out to both the Texas AG’s office and Oracle, but representatives did not immediately respond.

Who’s affected by the Oracle Health breach?

Oracle healthcare customers include hospitals and clinics in Texas and other states, as well as the Department of Defense and the Department of Veterans Affairs. Of the nearly 20 million people affected, 3 million were Texans.

Christus Health, a nonprofit healthcare system in Texas, and Tri-City Medical Center in California — both affected by the breach — said stolen patient data could include names, Social Security numbers, doctors, diagnoses, medicines and test results, Bloomberg reported.

Christus said that patients whose data was compromised would receive letters about the incident and also would be offered a complimentary two-year membership to credit monitoring and identity protection services.

 CyPro noted Tuesday that at least 29 hospital and health systems said they had been affected by the breach.

“The incident demonstrates how older infrastructure can remain a material source of third party risk during cloud migration,” Rob McBride, a CyPro founding partner, wrote. “Even though Oracle says its cloud infrastructure was unaffected, data held on two legacy servers was sufficient to expose information potentially belonging to millions of patients.”

What if your data was stolen?

Stolen data can be used to make scam attempts much more convincing, especially if the would-be criminals know your name, address or healthcare details, says Cliff Steinhauer, director of information security and engagement at the digital safety nonprofit National Cybersecurity Alliance.

“If someone contacts you claiming to be from insurance or a medical provider and asks for sensitive information or demands payment, hang up and call your provider back at a number you know belongs to them (like the back of your insurance card),” Steinhauer told CNET via email.

Steinhauer said that people whose data was stolen in the Oracle breach should find out what data was taken and use any identity or credit monitoring being offered.

“Keep an eye on your credit reports, financial accounts and healthcare statements for anything you don’t recognize,” he added. “It’s always a good idea to freeze your credit with all three major credit reporting bureaus as a preventative measure.”

fullText:
Good morning and happy October. Today, I’m cringing at this gaggle of billionaires pretending to be human, vibing to the new Tinashe album, Popstar, and heartily dining on all the brutal ‘Digger’ reviews.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

What year is it?

	

After months of waiting, Gemini 4 ‘Argon’ is finally out — sort of. Google unveiled the new state-of-the-art model late yesterday but has only made it available to “a set of trusted cyber defenders” while it undergoes testing. The company says it will get a wider release “as soon as possible.”

This is a big moment for Google. Many users and critics alike wrote it off completely, with one analysis firm saying “for all intents and purposes, we believe DeepMind is no longer a frontier lab.” While the company has released several useful, fast and affordable Flash-branded models in 2026, its latest salvo into state-of-the-art AI was back in November 2025 with Gemini 3 Pro. In fact, it was so good that for a brief time Google was considered to be well ahead of OpenAI and Anthropic, and presaged a “code red” inside the frontier labs.

It’s hard to overstate how important it is for Gemini 4 to succeed. After a massive executive shuffle in August saw Demis Hassabis and Jeff Dean removed from the core management team, most of DeepMind’s operations were shifted from London to Mountain View, where new head Koray Kavukcuoglu reports directly to Google CEO Sundar Pichai.

While there has been speculation that Google, with its entrenched customer base, would walk away from the frontier in favor of cheaper, more product-focused pursuits, Kavukcuoglu has refuted those rumors. Earlier this month, he said, “To put it very bluntly, there’s nothing other than being at the frontier that is important for us. We have the whole full stack… and we are able to optimize to be able to achieve our goals.”

According to benchmarks, Gemini 4 is competitive with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 in most tests, and is trained to be much better at agentic tasks than any previous Gemini model. It’s also better aligned, with a focus on cybersecurity, and has a massive 1M token output limit, which makes it far more capable of producing large bodies of work in one prompt with less compaction.

The big question, though, is whether Argon will be competitive in the real world. A Bloomberg report published shortly before the embargo lifted on the Gemini 4 news quoted anonymous Google employees skeptical of its coding abilities. From Bloomberg: “While Gemini 4 has performed well on benchmarks widely used to gauge model efficacy, it does less well when employees actually put it to work, according to people with direct access to the effort. The model struggles to handle certain coding tasks, said the people, who requested anonymity to discuss an internal matter.”

Argon is also curiously priced. Its introductory rate of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens matches OpenAI’s Sol 6.1 cost right now, but will eventually double to hit the $4/$20 price of Claude Opus 5.5. While still significantly cheaper than Astra or Fable, it has to prove its mettle with users before Google is welcomed back into the arms of the fickle AI masses.

title: Apple overtakes Samsung to lead European carrier smartphone sales in Q2, per report
snippet: A new report from Counterpoint Research shows that Apple overtook Samsung during the second quarter of 2026 to become the leading smartphone brand in Europe’s carrier channel, as operator sales held up better than the broader market. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new report from Counterpoint Research shows that Apple overtook Samsung during the second quarter of 2026 to become the leading smartphone brand in Europe’s carrier channel, as operator sales held up better than the broader market. Here are the details.

Apple helps carrier sales outperform broader European smartphone market

In a report published today, Counterpoint Research says smartphone sales through carriers in Europe declined 4% year-over-year in Q2 2026, compared with an 11% drop in the open market. Total smartphone sales, per the report, declined 8%.

Apple was a key driver of this shift, having overtaken Samsung as the market share leader of Europe’s operator channel. Motorola and vivo also contributed to the growth with some strategic positioning with key European operators.

Counterpoint says this is yet another result of rising memory costs, which have hit Europe’s low-end smartphone market particularly hard. Carrier sales, meanwhile, have held up better because they tend to skew toward higher-end devices and premium brands such as Apple, with more phones purchased on contract.

According to the report, Apple’s share of smartphone sales through European carriers rose from 33% in Q2 2025 to 37% in Q2 2026, while Samsung’s fell from 39% to 34% over the same period.

That said, Chinese brand vivo posted the biggest year-over-year increase in carrier sales, at 90%, while Motorola came in a distant second with 27% growth.

Here’s Jan Stryjak, Associate Director at Counterpoint Research, on these numbers:

“Smartphone sales through operators in Europe are typically more high-end than through the open market, as more are purchased on a contract. They are also more skewed towards more premium brands like Apple, Samsung, and Google. The collapse of the low-end of the smartphone market so far in 2026 because of the memory price crisis has therefore benefitted the operator channel, which has declined comparatively less than the open market.”

Stryjak added that he expects the carrier channel to continue gaining share over the “next few quarters as the lower end of the market continues to be impacted by the memory crisis.” He also noted that independent retailers have increased promotional activity compared to carriers, “which could mitigate some of the price rises and provide addition [sic] stimulus to the open market.”

title: SpaceX alumni nab $100M to rethink shipping with autonomous freight trains
snippet: Parallel Systems raised $100M to scale production of its autonomous electric rail vehicle, which can shuttle thousands of pounds of freight up to 500 miles.
fullText:
The railroad industry was one of the first to disrupt how the world worked with technology, but lately, innovation in freight railroading has amounted to little more than longer and longer trains.

That has led many railroads to abandon shorter routes, ceding a chunk of the $1 trillion surface freight market to trucking companies. But as diesel prices reach record highs, some of those very trucking companies are going bust, leaving a hole in the market. Recently, at least 16 trucking companies went bankrupt over only a few weeks.

Parallel Systems might have a way to keep freight moving while allowing railroads to recapture market share. The startup has developed a rail vehicle capable of moving over several tons of freight as far as 500 miles without an operator. If the company can scale production of its Panther vehicles, it stands to make railroads profitable over short hauls once again.

“Less than 500 miles is hard for railroads to do competitively,” Matt Soule, co-founder and CEO of Parallel Systems, told TechCrunch. “Our technology allows them to take some of that trucking, and it’s for the public’s benefit.” 

Because it runs on railroads, Parallel’s vehicle doesn’t contribute to traffic congestion, and because it’s battery powered, it doesn’t pollute. To scale manufacturing of its third-generation vehicle and speed the commercial rollout, Parallel Systems has raised a $100 million Series C led by AVP, with participation from Hillspire, Agility Global, Cobalt Capital, Anthos Capital, Congruent Ventures, Riot Capital, and Collaborative Fund.

Soule and his co-founders started Parallel Systems in 2020 after years at SpaceX, where they designed rocket avionics systems.

Parallel’s vehicles can travel either independently or in platoons, which tend to be shorter than typical trains. It’s an approach that bucks the prevailing strategy used by railroads, known as precision railroading: As the railroad industry has matured, investor pressure has driven companies to build longer trains and operate them on fixed schedules, which helps spread some costs like labor across more freight. 

As railroads have pulled back from smaller routes, trucking companies have stepped in. Today, some 60% of freight trips in the U.S. are under 500 miles, and trucking companies handle a majority of those.

But more trucks on the road means more congestion, and nowhere is that more apparent than at ports. “If you ever go to the Port of Savannah, you see the truck lines coming in and out of the port — it’s insanity,” Soule said. 

Unlike traditional train cars, Parallel’s vehicles don’t have couplers, instead forming uncoupled platoons that move down the rails. The coupler-free design means that, once a platoon reaches a train yard, the vehicles can split up without needing human intervention. And after the Panther is cleared to operate on a section of track, its sensors monitor the rails to ensure the track ahead is clear of obstacles.

Trucking companies have been intrigued by Parallel, despite the fact that the startup is claiming part of a business they currently own. Drayage companies, which move freight short distances, make money for each load they deliver, but they don’t get to charge more when a truck gets stuck in a traffic jam, even at a port where such congestion is common. By moving freight closer to a customer’s door, Parallel allows trucking companies to make more deliveries per day. “They want certainty, they want to be able to move,” Soule said.

Parallel obtained approval a year-and-a-half ago from the Federal Railroad Administration to operate near the Port of Savannah in Georgia, where it has been operating on 160 miles of track to prove the safety of its system. 

“We’ve been verifying all the safety controls and operating practices that are best evaluated in a real-world setting with a path toward our first commercial payload coming up very soon,” Soule said.

De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College.

title: Here’s everything we know so far about Apple’s next entry-level iPad: A19 chip, more
snippet: Apple’s current iPad, the A16 model, has gone untouched for well over a year. It remains the only device in Apple’s core product lineup without support for Apple Intelligence. Rumors had swirled for quite some time about an A18 model coming this year. Now, it’s sounding like Apple has an even bigger plan. more…
fullText:
Apple’s current iPad, the A16 model, has gone untouched for well over a year. It remains the only device in Apple’s core product lineup without support for Apple Intelligence. Rumors had swirled for quite some time about an A18 model coming this year. Now, it’s sounding like Apple has an even bigger plan.

It’s likely safe to assume that the delays with this product launch have much to do with the ongoing memory crisis affecting the electronics industry. It wouldn’t surprise me if Apple had the A18 refresh roadmapped for earlier this year alongside the debut of the M4 iPad Air, then had to push it.

As a reminder, Apple raised the price of the base iPad from $349 to $449 this summer alongside the rest of its memory-related price hikes. This brings it back to the price it initially launched at in 2022.

New iPad details

However, a new leak from MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris paints a more promising picture. Instead of utilizing the A18 chip, it sounds like the next entry-level iPad will equip the A19 chip. Alongside that, you’ll get the N1 networking chip, as well as the C1X modem on the cellular version. This’ll bring support for Wi-Fi 7 to Apple’s cheapest iPad.

The A19 iPad will also be equipped with 8GB of memory, allowing users to run Siri AI, though you’ll still miss out on the most capable local models and the more advanced dictation models, as those features require 12GB of memory. It’s not a major loss, but worth pointing out.

Another possibility is that the A19 iPad might offer a new name. With the debut of the MacBook Neo, Apple marketing exec Greg Joswiak pointed out that calling the MacBook Neo just “MacBook” would leave it without an identity. Hopefully, with the next entry-level iPad, we also get some sort of proper name like “SE” or “Neo” so we have something to call it.

Beyond that, don’t expect any sort of redesign or display improvements. There may be new colors, but probably nothing else. I personally wish Apple would bring USB 3 to the product, so users don’t have to suffer with such slow transfer speeds. It’d certainly help justify the new higher starting price.

Release date

	

Apple’s next budget iPad should be releasing next Spring, per Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. That’ll accompany other products like the M6 MacBook Air, A19 Pro MacBook Neo, M7 14-inch MacBook Pro, and more.

Are you someone in the market for the entry-level iPad? What are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.

title: iOS 27’s Siri gets one thing very right that other AI assistants get wrong
snippet: Siri AI is a major upgrade to Apple’s assistant that’s now available in iOS 27. And there’s one standout area I’ve noticed where it differs greatly from other AI assistants—for the better. more…
fullText:
Siri AI is a major upgrade to Apple’s assistant that’s now available in iOS 27. And there’s one standout area I’ve noticed where it differs greatly from other AI assistants—for the better.

iOS 27’s new Siri doesn’t pretend to be human, unlike every other AI chatbot

I’ve been using Siri AI for nearly four months, since the first iOS 27 beta launched. Overall, it’s checked all the boxes I was hoping for.

The new Siri is far more capable than its predecessor, delivering on the original promise of being a truly capable assistant on Apple devices.

I’ll admit though: if you need the most powerful, cutting-edge AI tool, you might be better served by competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini.

However, after using Siri AI and comparing it to those third-party tools, I’ve noticed a key difference where I greatly favor Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn’t pretend to be human.

It’s not overly verbose, mimicking a human-like personality that might lull you into forming a personal relationship with it.

Siri is helpful, intelligent, and does what you ask it to do. But the way it responds makes clear that it’s a tool, not a person. It reminds you regularly that it’s an AI, so it can make mistakes. And it won’t faux date you.

Whereas ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are all bursting with personality, opinions, and demonstrate more human-like tendencies in a way that, for me, feels disingenuous.

I imagine some users enjoy that more “personal” approach. But I much prefer that AI assistants stay in their lane and don’t pretend to be something they’re not.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. And I love that Apple gets that, and built the new Siri accordingly.

What’s your view of how “human-like” an AI assistant should be? Let us know in the comments.

title: Google stands by Gemini 4 performance as some claim it ‘struggles’ in real-world use
snippet: Google yesterday unveiled its new flagship Gemini 4 model with some impressive scores, but a report suggests that it might “struggle” in some cases. more…
fullText:
Google yesterday unveiled its new flagship Gemini 4 model with some impressive scores, but a report suggests that it might “struggle” in some cases.

Google announces Gemini 4 Argon as its new frontier model

Bloomberg reports that, internally, Google employees have found that Gemini 4’s real-world performance doesn’t always line up with its benchmark scores. During the unveiling of Gemini 4 Argon, Google showed that its new model outpaced competitors including OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra in many key areas.

The report cites Googlers who found that the model “does less well when employees actually put it to work,” and that it “struggles to handle certain coding tasks.” Google, speaking to Bloomberg on the claims, said that it “would be inaccurate to say that Gemini 4 is underperforming in areas such as coding,” also referencing comments from Koray Kavukcuoglu, the head of Google DeepMind, from late September, when he said that “it’s a certainty that we are always gonna be at the frontier.” The report cites one Googler who said that there’s a “large consensus” that Gemini 4 is at the frontier amongst employees, while others are concerned that Gemini “will still lag behind” competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI. Clearly, there’s a split in how employees view the model’s performance.

Gemini 4 Argon brings welcome upgrades to the model, including an expanded output limit of up to 1 million tokens, while Google also explained that the model is “highly capable at cybersecurity defense” and shows “leading performance” in other use cases. Gemini 4 Argon comes at a cost of “$4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens” but will see introductory pricing which is half of that.

title: Samsung officially raises Galaxy S26 prices by $100, but it hasn’t changed everywhere
snippet: Samsung is officially rolling out a price hike for the Galaxy S26 series, raising prices by $100 across the lineup. more…
fullText:
Samsung is officially rolling out a price hike for the Galaxy S26 series, raising prices by $100 across the lineup.

Effective immediately, the entire Galaxy S26 series is now $100 more expensive. Samsung had already raised prices on the base Galaxy S26 and the Galaxy S26+ compared to last year’s models, while the Ultra remained unchanged until now. 

The Galaxy S26 Ultra’s 1TB version sees the biggest price hike from $1,799 to $1,999.

The updated prices are already in place at Samsung.com, though third-party retailers such as Amazon and Best Buy have yet to update, though that’s likely only a matter of time.

	

Price updates are as follows:

256GB

512GB

1TB

Galaxy S26

$899 > $999

$1,099 > $1,199

N/A

Galaxy S26+

$1,099 > $1,199

$1,299 > $1,399

N/A

Galaxy S26 Ultra

$1,299 > $1,399

$1,499 > $1,599

$1,799 > $1,999

The Galaxy S26 FE, which just launched in August, does not appear to be going up in price at this time, with Samsung having already increased the price by $50 over the prior generation. Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Samsung’s other foldables are also not seeing higher prices.

While Samsung hasn’t issued a reason for the price hike, the rising cost of memory and other components is surely to blame – thanks RAMageddon (and all the AI).

title: Bloom raises $3.6M to become the ‘Alibaba’ of American manufacturing
snippet: The Detroit startup has widened its scope beyond mobility to help drone and robotics companies find U.S. based manufacturers, shippers, and more.
fullText:
When Justin Kosmides co-founded Bloom in 2023, his goal was to create a savior for the mobility industry. He had seen many e-bike and e-scooter companies fail because of an inability — or an unwillingness — to outsource some of the hardest problems, like logistics, manufacturing, or building a supply chain. He wanted to convince survivors and new entrants to let Bloom handle that work for them.

Then Donald Trump got re-elected and started shotgun-blasting tariffs on dozens of countries, partially to jump-start U.S. manufacturing. This accelerated a hardware scene that was already heating up in this country and, suddenly, it was more than just mobility companies looking to beef up their domestic supply chain. Robotics startups, drone-makers, and many more started to pop up.

That was an opportunity for Bloom, which is based in Detroit, but to tackle it, the startup had to partially reinvent itself. Instead of performing some of those harder, behind-the-scenes tasks, which was a big part of the original plan, Bloom shifted to a pure marketplace model, in which it connects buyers and sellers. It’s now focused on making, essentially, supply chain AI agents that Bloom’s customers use to find specific types of suppliers, parts, or manufacturing and engineering services.

The reinvention slowed Bloom’s fundraising plans. But the company has now made over 2,000 matches for more than 140 companies, and it wants grow faster. In an interview earlier this year, Kosmides, who is Bloom’s CEO, said his startup is like AI-driven version of Alibaba did in China, where it created a marketplace for contract manufacturers.

Investors are finally buying in. On Wednesday, Bloom announced a $3.6 million seed round led by SNAK Venture Partners, a marketplace-focused investment firm. Also joining were Flyover Capital (an early stage investor that focuses on flyover states), and deep tech firm Mana Ventures. Local backers included Detroit Venture Partners, Invest Detroit Ventures, and the Michigan Outdoor Innovation Fund.

Kosmides, sounding relieved, said in the interview that he’s “excited to be done with fundraising and get to back to building.”

No, then yes

SNAK first met with Bloom in April of last year, in the early stages of this reinvention. So early, in fact, that the firm passed on the chance to invest in the startup’s pre-seed round.

“We liked the founder and the thesis and passed anyway: we wanted to see more traction,” the firm wrote in a blog post. “We said so plainly and kept tracking the company.”

Bloom kept in touch with SNAK as it worked through becoming a more software-focused startup. By May of this year, Bloom had made as much revenue in five months as it did in all of 2025. SNAK also said the number of memberships on its platform had grown fivefold “with low churn,” meaning few customers were canceling.

“This is meant to reiterate that for us, a pass on pre-seed is not always a pass forever. We are fortunate to have a super focused thesis that allows us to track a small set of interesting early stage companies and build a relationship over time,” the firm wrote.

Kosmides said the fundraising scene has been a bit ruthless for startups like Bloom. Proving your value to investors in a world where the leading AI models keep improving can be an uphill battle. 

“To find investors to actually write a term sheet, not follow one, is getting harder and harder,” he said. “That’s just this new era that we’re in, with everyone trying to figure out what’s real and what’s not, what to invest in.”

Bloom did court other term sheets, Kosmides said. But SNAK, which was founded by longtime retail executive Sonia Nagar, is “who you want in your camp” to “build a hopefully category-defining marketplace for mobility, and drones, and all this hardware.” 

Matchmaking and discovery

Bloom’s platform handles both sides of a supplier relationship. Some customers use the platform to post contract opportunities, while others use it to bid on those opportunities. Bloom handles quoting, booking, and payment all on its platform, and it now helps match companies with suppliers that can do contract manufacturing, assembly, design and engineering, freight, warehousing, repairs, and even hazardous-materials shipping.

“Our friends at the parts marketplaces like Fictiv, Xometry, MacroFab and others are really good yesteryear marketplaces for finding one particular part,” Kosmides said. “But when you’re XYZ Drone Company, or an electric motorcycle company, and you need to find a provider that meets all these requirements have them all bid on this opportunity, that’s a lot more complicated than finding a CNC part.” 

Making this system work well is a big part Bloom’s reinvention, and it involved ingesting a lot of data about each provider on the platform. A lot of that was public data — how a company describes itself on its website, for instance. But around 30-40% of that data is coming directly from the companies, Kosmides said. Add in the data being generated as the startup onboards more customers and makes more matches, and you have Bloom’s edge, he said.

“You can build the craziest model for scraping data but you would never get to that accuracy,” he said. “We started with manually booking services, and then built in layers and pieces and understanding as we built up the provider network, as we built out more and more transactions, and so it’s only getting better and better.”

Kosmides believes this is all a better way to strike up supplier relationships, and that it also makes it easier for startups to get off the ground. But he also thinks Bloom’s platform will help create opportunities for small manufacturers who may not have big marketing budgets or sales teams.

He gave an example of one Michigan-based contract manufacturer that, until it started working with Bloom, was taking on odd jobs like refurbishing Nest thermostats and Bird scooters, or working with Chick-fil-A displays. That same company is now bidding on drone assembly contracts. 

“The ability to discover, and the ability to do matchmaking, that is what I think is truly missing” from U.S. manufacturing, he said. “That just doesn’t exist electronically.”

title: Samsung has updated these Galaxy devices to Android 17
snippet: Samsung is now rolling out its Android 17-based update, One UI 9, to its collection of supported Galaxy smartphones and tablets. Here’s the full list of devices that have been updated so far, and what you should know about the update. more…
fullText:
Samsung is now rolling out its Android 17-based update, One UI 9, to its collection of supported Galaxy smartphones and tablets. Here’s the full list of devices that have been updated so far, and what you should know about the update.

What’s new in Android 17 on Samsung Galaxy?

One UI 9, Samsung’s Android 17 update, continues the trend of evolution more than overhaul. The update introduces some slight design tweaks, more AI-powered features, and other changes built on the redesign that debuted in One UI 7 and was iterated in last year’s Android 16-based One UI 8. 

Some key changes in One UI 9 include:

Warranty & Samsung Care status in the Settings menu

Broader support for Now Nudge

My FanCam automatic video cropping based on a select subject

More Quick Panel (quick settings) customization

AI privacy alerts

Upgrades to Samsung DeX

New lock screen clocks that can adapt to your wallpaper

Samsung Galaxy devices with Android 17 – The full list

While Samsung hasn’t confirmed an exact schedule for its One UI 9 and Android 17 rollout for Galaxy devices, there are updates now rolling out in parts of the globe. Below you’ll find a regularly-updated list of every Samsung Galaxy device that has received a stable Android 17 update so far.

	

Galaxy S devices with Android 17

Galaxy S26

Galaxy S26+

Galaxy S26 Ultra

Galaxy S25 (limited availability)

Galaxy S25+ (limited availability)

Galaxy S25 Ultra (limited availability)

Galaxy S25 FE (limited availability)

Galaxy S25 Edge (limited availability)

Galaxy Z devices with Android 17

Galaxy Z Fold 7 (limited availability)

Galaxy Z Flip 7 (limited availability)

Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE (limited availability)

Galaxy Z TriFold (limited availability)

Updating…

One UI 9 changelog

Here’s the full changelog from Samsung for One UI 9, as listed for the Galaxy S26 series. Some features may vary by device.

Galaxy AI

Enhanced Now nudge

Now nudge provides helpful suggestions in more places throughout your Galaxy experience. In addition to the keyboard, suggestions will now appear in conversation notifications and in a floating button in the bottom right corner of the screen. There are also several new types of suggestions, like entering reservation details or addresses and saving places in Google Maps.

Focus on someone important

My FanCam lets you select a person in a video and follow them automatically while cropping out the rest of the video.

Interpreter keeps your conversation in front of you

In conversation mode, you can scroll through the whole conversation while you’re still talking.

See useful information during calls

See relevant events and other information related to your current call on the call screen.

Productivity and multitasking

More customizable quick panel

You can now rearrange and customize the controls in your quick panel even more than before. You can change the size of the brightness and volume sliders as well as the media player. You can also separate the sound mode button from the volume slider.

Privacy, security, and device protection

Warranty and care

The new Warranty and care menu in settings lets you check your warranty information and access diagnostic checks and useful information for keeping your Galaxy in top condition.

Lock down your phone quickly

It’s now easier to securely lock your phone in a hurry. Just press and hold the Volume down and Side buttons at the same time or tap the Power button in the quick panel. This prevents biometrics from being used the next time you unlock your phone.

Location access transparency

Stay on top of your location privacy. A blue indicator will appear at the top of the screen when an app accesses your location. Tap the indicator in the quick panel to see which app it is.

Stronger security and privacy protection

Alerts will appear in your Now brief to let you know about risks from malware, apps from unknown sources, unnecessary permissions, and other issues that may put your security and privacy at risk. Apps that have been identified as malicious or vulnerable will be blocked from opening until you make a decision about whether to remove them.

AI privacy alerts

Get help protecting your personal data. AI will monitor how apps use permissions and notify you about unnecessary access to your personal data.

Samsung Health

New look for Samsung Health

Samsung Health has been redesigned to make your health data easier to understand. Enjoy clearer visuals, improved charts, and a more engaging experience to help you reach your health goals.

Customize your Health home screen

Resize cards and organize them by category, like Activity, Sleep, Mindfulness, and Nutrition, so your top priorities are easy to access.

Log health data quickly

It’s now easier to add your health information right from the Samsung Health home screen. You can log your mood, meals, and more. You can even use the camera for faster input.

Advanced trend analysis

Track your progress with improved trend charts in Samsung Health. View data in hourly, daily, or weekly intervals, pinch to zoom in for a closer look, and overlay multiple charts to compare your performance across different periods.

Monitor changes in your sleep vitals

Samsung Health helps you notice meaningful changes in your sleep health data. Use Galaxy Watch or Ring measurements to better understand your daily health patterns.

Manage your heart health

Track key health metrics and lifestyle factors that affect your heart. A daily score based on your sleep, exercise, BMI, and blood pressure helps you better understand your current heart health trends.

Track your cardio load

See how your workouts and activity impact your heart so you’ll know when to push harder and when to rest. Your target cardio load range adjusts daily based on your recent activity and training focus.

Check your fitness index

Your Fitness Index is an overall score calculated using five key fitness metrics: body composition, cardio, strength, flexibility, and endurance. Set a goal and unlock personalized insights tailored to your results.

Keep your ears safe

The new Hearing tracker monitors sound levels detected by your Galaxy Watch and headphone audio levels to help you manage your exposure to loud sounds.

View your cycle and body rhythm

Get a more personalized view of your cycle and body rhythm with new cycle tracking options. You can view your cycle information in your calendar and better understand your health patterns.

Bixby

Activate Bixby with a gesture

Talk to Bixby just by raising your phone close to your mouth and speaking. No wake-up word needed.

Manage your conversations

Keep your chats organized. Search them, rename them, or pin your favorites. You can also delete all of your past conversations at once.

Bixby on the Home screen

Add a Bixby widget to type or talk to Bixby or jump directly to your conversation history.

Accessibility

Discover new Accessibility features

Check the What’s new menu in Accessibility settings to learn about and try the latest Accessibility features for your Galaxy.

Text spotlight for easier reading

Need a closer look? Tap any text on the screen to show it enlarged and highlighted in its own window. You can also customize the font size, colors, and other settings to match your preferences.

Physical keyboard shortcuts

Use shortcuts on your physical keyboard to access the Accessibility settings you need without touching the screen.

Mouse keys enhancements

New options are available when using your keyboard for mouse interactions including speed and acceleration control. You can also use the keyboard’s number pad to point and click.

Replace swipe with single tap

The Replace swipe with single tap option is now located in the Dexterity and interaction menu instead of the Assistant menu for easier access.

Select to speak

Get quick audio readouts without turning on full TalkBack. With the new Select to speak feature, you can select an item on your screen, like text or an image, and hear it read or described out loud.

Improved TalkBack updates

TalkBack updates can now be applied with a simple app update from the Play Store, helping you get the latest accessibility features and enhancements.

Even more improvements

New Lock screen clock

The default clock on your Lock screen has been redesigned with a cleaner and more modern look that adapts to match your wallpaper.

Samsung DeX enhancements

It’s easier to move an app window from one desktop to another using the menu at the top of the window. Desktop previews are now available at the top of the Recents screen, making it easier to switch with a single tap.

title: Samsung just raised the price on several more Galaxy phones in the US
snippet: Alongside a price hike on the Galaxy S26 series, Samsung has rolled out quiet price hikes on a number of its other Galaxy phones in the US as RAMageddon rages on. more…
fullText:
Alongside a price hike on the Galaxy S26 series, Samsung has rolled out quiet price hikes on a number of its other Galaxy phones in the US as RAMageddon rages on.

As component costs continue to skyrocket, price hikes are becoming the norm. Just in the past 24 hours we’ve seen prices go up on Samsung’s Galaxy S26 flagships as well as the 7-year-old Nvidia Shield TV Pro. Seemingly nothing is safe, and that includes more of Samsung’s Galaxy phones, too.

Through Samsung.com and other retailers, the price of several Galaxy A devices has gone up. 

This affects Galaxy A57, Galaxy A37, Galaxy A27, and Galaxy A17, with price adjustments ranging from $20 to $70 depending on the model and configuration.

	

Galaxy A57 (128GB): $549 $599

Galaxy A57 (256GB): $609 $679

Galaxy A37 (128GB): $449 $489

Galaxy A37 (256GB): $539 $609

Galaxy A27: $349 $379

Galaxy A17: $249 $269

PhoneArena, which first highlighted the price changes, also notes that this is the second major price hike on the Galaxy A17. Samsung’s entry-level device launched in January for $199 – and it arguably wasn’t even worth that price, let alone over 35% more.

But AI is just great, isn’t it?

fullText:

Meta’s AI agent now properly supports the iPad’s larger screen and recent improvements to multitasking.

Meta’s AI agent now properly supports the iPad’s larger screen and recent improvements to multitasking.

by  Andrew Liszewski

Oct 7, 2026, 3:37 PM UTC

Image: Meta

Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

After launching nearly a month ago and spending several weeks as the top free app in Apple’s App Store, the latest update to Meta’s Muse iOS app introduces native support for the iPad. A Mac version of Meta’s agentic AI tool (designed to compete with OpenClaw, ChatGPT’s Dots, and Grok Bot) was released about a week after the original mobile version debuted expanding its usefulness to desktop tasks like organizing files. The new iPad version should function similar to Muse on iPhones, but better take advantage of the extra screen real estate and iPadOS’ better multitasking capabilities.

The newly added iPad support is limited to just a one line mention at the bottom of the release notes for the latest version of Muse alongside several other updates for the iPhone version too. These include the ability to connect Muse to additional software tools like Canva, Dropbox, Figma, QuickBooks, GitHub, Zoom, Asana, and Klaviyo, and new connectors for apps like Granola and Notion. The new updates target small business owners with the option to give Muse a business goal which the agent will use to autonomously plan marketing, client pitches, and developing “new product pages.”

While it took Meta 15 years to release a dedicated version of Instagram for the iPad, the faster turnaround for Muse properly supporting Apple’s tablets is a clear indicator of the company’s strong support for its AI initiatives. Meta also recently announced a standalone Tamagotchi-like device called the Muse Charm that will run the AI agent without the need for a smartphone, and it’s working to bring Muse to its smart glasses.
