title: Googlebook Glowbar doesn’t have the ‘knock-knock’ Chromebook Pixel battery gesture
snippet: One of the beloved features of Google’s original big push into laptops, the Chromebook Pixel, is getting a revival in Googlebook’s Glowbar, but it very much feels like a hollow version of what came before. more…
fullText:
One of the beloved features of Google’s original big push into laptops, the Chromebook Pixel, is getting a revival in Googlebook’s Glowbar, but it very much feels like a hollow version of what came before.

The original Chromebook Pixel launched in 2013 as the launchpad for ChromeOS. To this day, it remains a pretty incredible piece of hardware design, though it was inherently flawed with a truly atrocious display and a sky-high price tag to boot, not to mention an even more restricted operating system compared to what ChromeOS would eventually morph into. Still, it earned a follow-up in 2015’s Chromebook Pixel which delivered a lot of key upgrades.

Both models included a signature hardware feature in the four-piece “light bar” across the top of the lid. It was mainly a design element to ring in the Chrome connection with the four colors of the Chrome and Google logos. It lived on in the later, yet short-lived Pixel C tablet. 

It also served a somewhat practical purpose, too.

	

When you would plug in a Chromebook Pixel, the light bar would give you a rough idea of how much charge was already in the battery. Beyond that, a fun little “knock-knock” gesture on the lid would tell you the same information, but whenever the laptop was just out. You could tap the lid and get an idea of the battery status without opening it up or plugging it in, which was especially useful in a time where laptop battery was still very much Not Great.

It’s that gesture that’s gone on Googlebook’s Glowbar, which retains the light-up action when you plug it in, but loses the “knock-knock” that really grabbed everyone’s attention when Google first launched it. 

What can the Glowbar do? 

Like Chromebook Pixel, it does light up when you plug the machine into power, showing battery status both when it plugged in and unplugged. Useful! It’s also more granular than it was on that older hardware. The only other function, besides an animation when you close the lid, is interaction with Gemini. I struggle to see the utility in that one given the Glowbar is at the back of the display, but I guess why not?

title: Google Labs announces ‘Playground’ for prompt-based game creation
snippet: Google today announced an “experimental gaming platform” called Playground that lets you “create, play, and share” browser-based games. The goal is to “make game creation more approachable and ignite everyday creativity.” more…
fullText:
Google today announced an “experimental gaming platform” called Playground that lets you “create, play, and share” browser-based games. The goal is to “make game creation more approachable and ignite everyday creativity.”

This Google Labs experiment leverages  Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria models with a “custom harness to make game creation more accessible.”

It starts with a chat interface that lets you “direct the game just by typing what you want to build.” You can decide between a 2D or 3D game and specify whether it’s single or multi-player. Google offers starter prompts that you can remix and a guided development experience.

Playground lets you “tweak the physics, rewrite the rules, customize the characters, or overhaul the environment.”

	

Google today also previewed a Unity Spark integration that allows for “robust, professional-level mechanics, high-fidelity 3D capabilities, and the flexibility of the Unity runtime.”

The accessibility of Playground and world-class game-building expertise of Unity provides the building blocks for an ecosystem where users can start with a simple text prompt and eventually grow into building immersive experiences with Unity

These are browser-based games that are playable on phone or laptop. Once you’re done, games can be kept private, shared via link, or published to the Playground Explore gallery for everyone. Titles go through safety (community guideline) screening along with user reporting.

Players can rate games, while there’s support for in-game leaderboards with Play Games profile integration.

Google is rolling out Playground starting in the US. Free users will be able to generate games, with expanded access tied to Google One membership.

snippet: This week Apple refreshed its third-party accessories lineup to include eight additional products. This includes the Aqara Thermostat Hub W200 and more. more…
fullText:
This week Apple refreshed its third-party accessories lineup to include eight additional products. This includes the Aqara Thermostat Hub W200 and more.

Aqara first launched the Thermostat Hub W200 in April after being unveiled at CES 2026 in January.

The Aqara Thermostat Hub W200 retails for $169.95 at Apple. While that’s $10 more than Amazon’s price, it may be helpful if you have Apple credit to spend or you’re already shopping from Apple.

Apple adding it to its online and retail stores is a strong endorsement. It’s also notable for Apple Home-specific features like Apple Adaptive Temperature and Clean Energy Guidance

title: Spotify’s New Music Quiz Will Test Your Trivia Knowledge
snippet: Spotify now has quizzes for over 2,000 artists, and you can share the results with your friends.
fullText:
How well do you know your music trivia? Music streaming service Spotify has unveiled a new mobile feature called Music Quiz that tests fans’ knowledge of over 2,000 artists. It’s rolling out to the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and a handful of other countries from Tuesday.

The shareable quiz, which follows a BTS quiz earlier in the year, features music trivia, album cover art and audio tracks spanning an artist’s music and milestones. Fans can share their scores for each artist’s quiz with friends, like the popular New York Times puzzle Wordle.

There are quizzes for artists including Bad Bunny, Don Toliver, Bruno Mars and Charli xcx.

			

More from CNET

Read more: Best Music Streaming Service of 2026

How to use the Spotify Music Quiz

To find a music quiz, you have to go to the individual artist’s page.

First, make sure your Spotify app is up to date.

Next, play a track from the artist, and a Music Quiz card will pop up in their profile.

The app will then ask a series of questions about the artist and their music, and once you’ve finished, you can share your score on various social media and messaging apps.

Spotify is the world’s largest music streaming service, with over 300 million paid subscribers. It frequently experiments with new ways of engaging its users, including snapshots of your music streaming history, AI-driven personalization options, a Running Mode for your workouts and the popular Wrapped yearly summary.

title: Apple killed the Mac mini’s best hidden feature [Video]
snippet: With the release of the M6 Mac mini and its more powerful M5 Pro counterpart, Apple quietly killed off one of the machine’s most compelling features. While both new Mac mini models look like their predecessors from the outside, Apple nixed the hidden feature that made the previous-generation Mac mini an incredible value. more…
fullText:
With the release of the M6 Mac mini and its more powerful M5 Pro counterpart, Apple quietly killed off one of the machine’s most compelling features. While both new Mac mini models look like their predecessors from the outside, Apple nixed the hidden feature that made the previous-generation Mac mini an incredible value.

When it first launched, the M4 Mac mini provided a huge bang for the buck. Not only did it feature Apple’s M4 SoC, but it also came with a healthy 16GB of unified memory, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, two front-facing USB 3 ports, HDMI, and Ethernet. At just $599 or $499 at the student discount price, the M4 Mac mini was not only the most versatile Mac in Apple’s lineup but also, pound for pound, the best Mac in the lineup. 

Subscribe to 9to5Mac on YouTube for more videos

But Apple’s smallest Mac had a secret up its sleeve that made it an even more valuable machine: a slot for upgradable storage. Users could literally pry open the machine’s back cover, unscrew a few screws, and access a removable NAND module that could be easily replaced with a third-party SSD up to 2TB.

The benefits were multifaceted. Not only could you upgrade the SSD or easily fix a drive that failed, but you could also save some serious coin by forgoing Apple’s build-to-order upgrade option and do it yourself with a much cheaper third-party SSD. 

Upgrading the M4 Mac mini SSD

At the time, Apple charged $800 for the 2TB upgrade, transforming the “budget” computer into a $1400 computer with the click of an option. By upgrading after purchase with a third-party SSD, users could save nearly $500.

Of course, as someone who likes to tinker, I was extremely excited about this and ended up posting a full video tutorial showing, step by step, how to upgrade the stock SSD with a third-party drive. It proved to be quite popular, amassing half a million views. 

Video: How to upgrade the M4 Mac mini SSD

It was nice while it lasted.

With the launch of this latest generation of Mac mini, Apple has soldered the SSD directly to the logic board, effectively eliminating the ability to upgrade it post-purchase with a third-party NAND module.

The Mac mini has gone from what was hands-down the best bang-for-your-buck Mac to a significantly more expensive product, not just for the base model, which goes from $600 to $900, but also for the 2TB upgrade, which goes from $800 to $1000. 

Today if you want an M6 Mac mini with a 2TB SSD, you’ll need to pay Apple $1900. The equivalent M4 Mac mini, with a 2TB aftermarket upgrade, would have set you back roughly $920 when you factor in the $320 aftermarket upgrade price being charged at the time. Obviously, things have gotten more expensive, so it’s not exactly Apple’s to Apple’s (see what I did there), but that’s a $1000 increase in price, not only because Apple is charging significantly more, but also because Apple eliminated the ability for customers to upgrade the machines themselves.

I have a good idea as to why Apple opted to increase the price of the base Mac mini by $300, and I can even understand why its SSD prices have increased so much. Because of AI and other factors, component, SSD, and memory prices have all skyrocketed. But that doesn’t explain why Apple opted to solder the SSDs to the logic board instead of keeping them user-replaceable like before.

	

We can speculate, but we may never know the real answer for Apple’s decision to revert back to soldered SSDs. What we do know, however, is that these machines are significantly more expensive, and even that sounds like an understatement. In the case of the M4 Mac mini with a 2TB aftermarket upgrade vs the M6 Mac mini with a 2TB build-to-order upgrade, it’s roughly a 106% price increase.

9to5Mac’s Take

It can be difficult to find a base model M4 Mac mini on the used market at a reasonable price, but if you can manage to do so, it remains an excellent machine for its baseline performance, features, and upgradable SSD.

The good news in all of this is that all of Apple’s Mac mini models come with Thunderbolt connectivity, so you can easily add high-bandwidth external storage via a USB or Thunderbolt SSD. I’m personally a big fan of the Samsung T9, which offers a relatively affordable way to add extra storage. 

What do you think Apple’s reasoning is for getting rid of user-replaceable SSDs in the Mac mini? Do you have any particular theories? Sound off in the comments with your thoughts.

title: Motorola is rolling out its Android 17 update to more devices

fullText:

Motorola’s condensed changelog notes a “fresh, expressive design” and “smarter notifications,” both of which were detailed in a previous detailed overview of the update.

title: Googlebook’s Android-integrated features won’t work with Samsung phones at launch
snippet: Googlebook is pitched as the laptop for Android users but, at launch, the vast majority of Android users can’t use the platform’s best features. more…
fullText:
Googlebook is pitched as the laptop for Android users but, at launch, the vast majority of Android users can’t use the platform’s best features.

Built on top of Android, Googlebook’s core pitch is to be the laptop for Android users, with deep integration between your smartphone and laptop. This includes a host of features such as instant hotspot, notification sync, phone file access, and the ability to continue tasks started on your phone from your Googlebook laptop. You can also stream apps from your phone’s display to your Googlebook directly.

In terms of deep integration, is a good pitch, but it won’t work for a lot of users at launch.

On a support page, Google confirms that Googlebook’s suite of Android integrations won’t work with any device running Android 16 or prior – Android 17 is the minimum requirement. 

	

Beyond that, Google also confirmed that Samsung devices are not supported at launch. Rather, support is rolling out “over the coming weeks.” It’s not mentioned whether Google or Samsung needs to push an update here, but it stands to reason that an update on Samsung’s end might be needed.

Support for Better Together features will be rolling out across all Android 17-supported Samsung devices over the coming weeks. Sorry for the inconvenience!

Meanwhile, Googlebook faces some other early hiccups, such as lacking support for Slack’s web app at launch, a key workplace app, as well as some apparent optimization issues for apps running on Intel hardware.

title: Claude launches Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides integration with sidebar and more
snippet: If Gemini isn’t quite your cup of tea, Anthropic’s Claude now supports sidebar integration with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides. more…
fullText:
If Gemini isn’t quite your cup of tea, Anthropic’s Claude now supports sidebar integration with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides.

You can already use Gemini natively in Google Workspace apps, but those invested in Claude can now use their AI of choice inside of Google’s ecosystem through the Claude for Google Workspace add-on which is in public beta starting today. A sidebar opens up alongside your file in Docs, Sheets, or Slides and can assist in building out documents, making edits, and more.

In Google Docs, Anthropic says you can use Claude integration to fix spelling, rewrite portions of a document, or restyle sections, all without breaking existing formatting. In Sheets, you can have Claude write formulas or build tables using the context of the document, or even upload extra documents/spreadsheets to build something new in Sheets. In Slides, Claude can build new slides using existing layouts or themes or flag elements that might need to be updated. Gemini can do much of this but, as mentioned, this is useful for those already invested in Claude.

There’s an “ask before edits” mode where Claude will let you preview changes before they’re made.

	

The Claude for Google Workspace beta is available to all paid Claude users through the Google Workspace marketplace. There are also new Claude connectors for Docs, Sheets, and Slides that let you edit Google Workspace files directly from Claude itself just by pasting a file link into your conversation with the AI.

fullText:
Do you remember the first time you backed out of the driveway on your own? It was pure freedom. For your parents? It was probably one of the most terrifying times of their life. When you were a teenager, your parents had no way to know how fast you were driving, when you arrived at your location, how safe you drove, etc. No news was good news, and hope was the only real tool available until you checked in with them. 

If you have teenage drivers today, rejoice in the fact that the fear of the unknown your parents had is not the world you have to live in today. There’s a lot of negatives with 2026 technology, but HeyPolo is a clear example of where technology has made life better and safer for teenage drivers.

HeyPolo is way more than just a paid version of Apple’s Find My service

HeyPolo is a family safety app that covers real-time location sharing, arrival and departure alerts, SOS emergency alerts, and driving safety features all in one single app for one price. The driving piece is what sets it apart from a basic location sharing app like Apple’s Find My service. Every trip your teenage driver takes is tracked and scored, and you can see exactly how it went: how fast they drove, whether they were using their smartphone behind the wheel, whether there was sudden braking or rapid increases in speed, and whether any serious driving events were detected.

The Driving Score gives each trip a number based on their actual driving behavior, so you’re not just guessing whether your teen is actually driving safely. You can see the data, have a real conversation about it if it’s going poorly, and watch the score improve over time as their habits improve. It’s a much more useful tool for actually helping a new driver get better than anything that was available a generation ago.

Crash detection, arrival alerts, and so much more

HeyPolo detects crashes and notifies you automatically. Which, with combined with arrival alerts that fire when your teenager gets to school, sport practice, to a friends, or home, you go from hoping that no news is good news to actually knowing if they are safe or not. You don’t have to wait on them to text or call when they arrive. You’ll know exactly when they do, and that’s a peace of mind for parents that is worth its weight in gold. HeyPolo updates locations on a 5 second interval, so your their location is always accurate.

The whole family for one price

One HeyPolo subscription covers your entire family with absolutely no per-person fees. It works great across iPhone and Android, so a mixed-device household isn’t a problem. HeyPolo is built by the team behind Surfshark, which means there’s serious privacy infrastructure behind it as well. They don’t sell your data, you control what you share with who and when it stops, and all data is deleted every 7 days. With a location based application, this is a critical privacy aspect.

There’s no reason not to try out HeyPolo out as it comes with a 30-day money-back guarantee, and there’s no lock-in if you decide it’s not for you and your family.

title: Google Find Hub tags adding NFC support, better registration
snippet: According to the latest version of Google Play services, Find Hub tags are getting two new capabilities. more…
fullText:
According to the latest version of Google Play services, Find Hub tags are getting two new capabilities.

Version 26.39 of Google Play services has two Security & Privacy features related to the Find Hub network.

[Phone] With NFC support, you can quickly access Find Hub tag details and settings or identify lost tags when you tap the tag with your phone.

Find Hub devices that support NFC can be tapped with a phone to reveal “details and settings or identify lost tags.” At the moment, you have to place lost tags in an identification mode to get details, with the process varying between products. Tapping would be much easier.

NFC is not a common feature on Find Hub trackers. For example, it’s absent on the upcoming Pixel Tag. The Xiaomi Tag released earlier this year has NFC, but it appears limited to Apple’s Find My network. That said, Play services adding this support suggests such devices are coming.

	

[Phone] With the new registration flow, you can now set categories, rename tags, and configure features like Left-Behind Reminders when you first set up your Find Hub network tags, so you don’t have to configure them manually in the app later.

The second update introduces an improved setup process. It lets you set a category (Bag, Bike, Car, etc.), rename tags, and control other settings when you first register a device. Previously, you had to open the Find Hub app to do all this.

title: Tim Cook sold nearly $63.9 million in Apple shares this month
snippet: Apple executive chair and former CEO Tim Cook sold nearly 200,000 Apple shares on October 2, one day after more than 374,000 restricted stock units vested as part of his compensation package. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple executive chair and former CEO Tim Cook sold nearly 200,000 Apple shares on October 2, one day after more than 374,000 restricted stock units vested as part of his compensation package. Here are the details.

As reported by Investing.com (via MacMagazine), Tim Cook sold 191,753 Apple shares on October 2, following the settlement of 374,541 restricted stock units (RSUs) on October 1.

RSUs are a form of stock-based compensation that entitle an employee to receive company shares once certain conditions are met. In Cook’s case, the number of shares that vested was determined by Apple’s total shareholder return relative to other S&P 500 companies over a three-year period.

According to the filing, Cook’s shares were sold across multiple transactions at prices ranging from $330.66 to $334.50 per share. At the time of publication, Apple stock was trading at $333.84 per share.

The report adds:

Apple withheld 199,038 shares, valued at $65,746,232 based on a price of $330.32 per share, to cover tax withholding requirements related to the RSU vesting.

Investing.com notes that the sale was carried out under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan that Cook adopted in May, meaning the transaction had been arranged in advance rather than decided on the day of the sale.

Cook also transferred 26,325 Apple shares as a gift on October 2, although the filing does not identify the recipient.

Even after the sale, the tax withholding, and the gifted shares, Cook still holds more than 3.2 million Apple shares through his trust.

title: The Pixel 4 is still my favorite Google smartphone hardware, and it holds up
snippet: Google Pixel has evolved tremendously over the years, with some radically different designs showing up between generations. As the lineup turns 10, the Pixel 4 remains the one that stands out as my favorite smartphone hardware Google has made yet, and it’s not just about the looks. more…
fullText:
Google Pixel has evolved tremendously over the years, with some radically different designs showing up between generations. As the lineup turns 10, the Pixel 4 remains the one that stands out as my favorite smartphone hardware Google has made yet, and it’s not just about the looks.

Elephant in the room: The Pixel 4 series is objectively the worst pair of smartphones Google ever released. Funny, given that the beloved Pixel 4a came out of it, but it’s impossible to argue that Google nailed it here. Following up on its Pixel 3 series which, at the time, was the first launch that really started gainig traction, the Pixel 4 took a big swing in practically every way and it did not work.

But for all of its failings, the Pixel 4 remains my favorite piece of hardware overall.

Why?

	

I think this is the most unique smartphone Google made, and also the one most meant for actual people to use it. The looks themselves aren’t exactly groundbreaking. The mostly blank back with a single square camera module is relatively generic by today’s standards. I’ll still vouch for “Oh So Orange” any day – and still actively regret not keeping mine – but I’d also argue there’s beauty in the simplicity here. It’s timeless.

Of course, less timeless is that big forehead over the display. Used to house the Soli sensor and face unlock hardware, this was another place where Google made a big swing that didn’t work out. Fundamentally, I don’t think Google made a mistake here. The face unlock sensor still works, and even recognized me with a beard that I didn’t have 7 years ago when I was actively using this phone. Impressive! I still think I prefer Google’s forehead design to Apple’s iPhone notch of the time, but the cleverness of Apple’s Dynamic Island is way better than Google’s solution here. But with newer Pixels splitting the difference between security and hardware on face unlock, I think we’re in a pretty good spot nowadays. 

But what really lets the Pixel 4’s hardware live rent-free in my head is how it feels.

Again, for all of this phone’s failings, the physical hardware is truly just so nice. The soft-touch matte of the back panel hasn’t been replicated, and the visually contrasting side rails not only look great, but feel incredible in the hand. These really feel like they were born out of Google’s cozy, human take to product design of the time and I wish the company had continued down that path. 

Don’t get me wrong, the modern Pixel design is gorgeous. I’m a big fan of the camera bar and Google’s approach to color, but the aesthetic of the Pixel 4 is something that I wish we’d seen more of. It was such a great foundation that felt not just unique, but better at the time.

	

Of course, that was largely ruined by the shortcomings. Pixel 4’s legacy is largely around being too expensive, ditching a fingerprint sensor at exactly the wrong time, and truly atrocious battery life. 

Still, if I had any influence whatsoever over the next 10 years of Pixel design, stop number one would be revisiting some of the core design ideas behind the Pixel 4.

What do you think?

title: Here’s how much Google is testing paying web publishers for AI Overview usage
snippet: A new report details how Google is testing paying web publishers for content used in its AI Overviews, including how much they’re making and how much that varies. more…
fullText:
A new report details how Google is testing paying web publishers for content used in its AI Overviews, including how much they’re making and how much that varies.

Google’s AI Overviews have drastically reshaped the web, and it’s hard to argue that it hasn’t harmed publishers across the web. Traffic is down almost universally, though Google insists AI isn’t to blame. Still, Google’s AI Overviews and other AI responses rely on publishers around the web to continue operating, something that’s increasingly difficult to do.

Following a report earlier this month, The Information is now offering a few more details on Google’s test to directly pay web publishers when their content is used in AI Overviews. 

The company is apparently paying around 100 digital publishers including “small to midsize blogs and websites.” Revenue seems to vary wildly, though. For some, it amounts to “less than one-tenth of 1% of their advertising revenue.” Some “smaller sites” have apparently earned less than $1,000 over several months, where another publisher that “joined a few months ago” has already made around $50,000-60,000 so far, “which doesn’t represent that much of its business.” Yet, another publisher said that a “bigger slice” was covered with Google’s payments earning “more than $1 million a year.”

	

The test, as previously reported, gives publishers insights into how often AI Overviews leverage their content. What’s not yet clear is how Google determines how much a publisher is paid, with some finding that “less widely covered” topics that “draw strong user interest” currently earn more, with examples including anime and gaming. 

It’s still unclear if Google plans to expand this program, but The Information reiterates that Google “needs these web publishers to stay active” for its models and answers to stay current and accurate.

title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon as its new frontier model
snippet: Gemini 4 Argon is Google’s “next era of frontier intelligence” and built for “deep reasoning across complex, long-horizon workflows.” It follows the cancellation of Gemini 3.5 Pro and focus on 3.8 Flash. more…
fullText:
Gemini 4 Argon is Google’s “next era of frontier intelligence” and built for “deep reasoning across complex, long-horizon workflows.” It follows the cancellation of Gemini 3.5 Pro and focus on 3.8 Flash.

With this new model (which has a new naming scheme), Google wants to offer “frontier-level capabilities” across coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity defense, and creative writing.

Gemini 4 Argon’s output token limit is 1M tokens (up from 64K) to allow for longer and more complex use cases. This is paired with expanded coding, reasoning, and multimodal capabilities.

When the model has the headroom to think deeply and generate hundreds of thousands of tokens in a single trajectory, it adds a new level of depth in reasoning to solve tough problems in one go.

In terms of benchmarks, Google touts a DeepSWE v1.1 score of 77.9%. Claude Opus 5.5 comes in at 74.2% followed by GPT-6 Astra’s 74.1%.

	

Google trained Gemini 4 Argon to be “highly capable at cybersecurity defense” with leaps over 3.8 Flash Cyber. The model will be made available “without cyber guardrails” to trusted defenders and internal Google teams so that they can “leverage its full frontier-level cybersecurity defense capabilities.”

“On CWE-bench v1, which evaluates the model’s ability to remediate security vulnerabilities, Argon ties for first place with a top score of 68%”

Outside of coding, Gemini 4 Argon also has “leading performance across other domain specific evaluations,” such as Vals Finance Agent v2 (multi-step financial research) and Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (legal research and drafting).

“On AutomationBench, Zapier’s benchmark measuring end-to-end execution across core business functions, Argon ranks #1 with a score of 51.3%.”

“…on LVBench, which measures long video understanding, Argon is state of the art with a score of 91.7%.”

Gemini 4 Argon is “rolling out soon,” starting with Google AI Ultra subscribers and paid API customers. 

“Argon will launch at an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off input token price.”

“After the introductory period expires, the price of $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens will apply.”

So far, it has been made available to trusted testers and cyber defenders (via Fairwind Program). Before the broader release, Google is focusing on:

Defending against misuse from cyber or chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) attacks: Google has improved “techniques to monitor the model’s internal activations to spot misuse.”

Defending against prompt injection attacks: Google’s “most resilient model yet against indirect prompt injections” with “leading in prompt injection robustness on the Gray Swan’s Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) Benchmark.”

Hardening systems: “we are hardening our sandboxed environments by isolating and sealing them before high-risk training or evaluations begin.”

Monitoring for misalignment: Google is “deploying misalignment mitigations that monitor Argon’s chain-of-thought and actions and stop execution when necessary.”

“We used a similar system to monitor our training runs and send alerts to a dedicated incident response team, taking careful precautions against feeding the findings back into training so as to not risk shaping Argon’s reasoning to evade our monitoring.”

Inside Google, Gemini 4 Argon is already powering internal workflows with “thousands of Googlers highlighting the model’s strengths in specialized coding tasks, conducting deeper research, and writing quality.” The company shared some examples today:

Memory efficiency: A team of Argon agents analyzed fleet-wide profiling telemetry to autonomously identify and apply memory optimizations across Google’s data centers, freeing up over 300 TiB of memory once rolled out, with an estimated 500 TiB to 1 PiB in total savings.

Large Scale Codebase Migrations and Optimizations: Argon agents are working on migrating C/C++ codebases to Rust across Google—scaling from tens of thousands of lines in core libraries like re2, libgav1 up to 800K+ lines for the Fuchsia OS Zircon kernel. Given the criticality of many of these systems, such large-scale rewrites are undergoing rigorous automated and manual auditing, emulation testing, and review before rolling out to production.

For libgav1, Google’s open source software for decoding video, Argon agents took an existing Rust port and replaced 32K lines of SIMD code by running many rounds of profile-guided experiments, studying the compiler’s output, producing safe Rust so the compiler would vectorize it automatically. The end result is a memory-safe video decoder that runs 2.7x faster than the Rust port, with identical video output, bringing it closer to the optimized C++.

macOS 27.2 beta 3 rolls out to developers

Two weeks ago, Apple rolled out the second developer beta of macOS 27.2 Golden Gate and, soon after that, the first public beta with the same build.

title: New Apple TV 4K launches next week with two major upgrades
snippet: New Apple products are reportedly launching on October 13, including an updated Apple TV 4K. Here are the two major upgrades rumored for the new Apple TV. more…
fullText:
New Apple products are reportedly launching on October 13, including an updated Apple TV 4K. Here are the two major upgrades rumored for the new Apple TV.

#1: Siri AI

When Siri AI was first unveiled by Apple this June, the company presented it as a cross-platform revamp that would work the same regardless of the device you’re using.

The new Siri debuted on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro. But curiously, there’s never been mention made of Siri AI on Apple TV or HomePod. And out of all the OS 27 updates that shipped last month, tvOS and HomePod software are the only ones missing the new Siri.

But that’s about to change, with Siri AI reportedly a tentpole addition to the new Apple TV 4K.

Based on what we’ve seen with Siri AI on other platforms, it’s set to be a big upgrade for tvOS users. In addition to increased intelligence around TV shows and movies, better content recommendations, and likely powering an improved InSight feature, the new Siri should also support asking world knowledge questions like any other device.

#2: A19-class chip, up from current A15 Bionic

The Apple TV 4K hasn’t been updated since 2022, and that model has an A15 chip that debuted in 2021.

But rumors indicate the new Apple TV 4K being unveiled next week will bring a big chip upgrade, boasting an A19 or A19 Pro chip.

	

Leaker Aaron Perris discovered a reference to the new hardware model in Apple code with an ‘AppleTV18,1’ identifier. This ‘18,1’ numbering scheme was also used for the iPhone 17 line, thus pointing to an A19-class chip being used.

I suspect it will be an A19 Pro rather than A19, since the latter doesn’t support the ability to customize Siri AI’s voice pace and expressivity. With Siri AI being a major focal point of the new Apple TV, the A19 Pro seems a safer bet.

title: Google Docs and Drive now support markdown files natively
snippet: Spurred by the use of markdown files in the AI age, Google Drive and Google Docs are adding full, native support for markdown (.md) files. more…
fullText:
Spurred by the use of markdown files in the AI age, Google Drive and Google Docs are adding full, native support for markdown (.md) files.

Google has been building out markdown support in Drive for years now, but prior steps largely included converting markdown into a format that Docs could use.

Now, Google Drive and its suite of apps can open, edit, and fully use markdown files throughout Docs and other apps. This includes real-time editing and comments with full rendering of the formatting of markdown documents. Google also points out that this benefits AI use cases such as having AI agents collaborate on documents and even syncing with Gemini Notebook.

Google explains:

	

Now that users can handle markdown files natively in Google Docs, they can open, edit, and collaborate on markdown files without changing the file type. Editing Markdown files in Docs also enables both users and agents to collaborate without forcing anyone to write raw syntax, handle manual file conversions, or give up Docs’ real-time editing and commenting tools.

Drive also now supports rendered markdown, so you can view fully formatted, beautiful documents with clickable links and structured tables right in Drive.

Google’s Chandu Thota calls out that markdown “has become the common language between humans and AI agents.”

Markdown support in Google Drive and Docs is rolling out starting today but may take up to 15 days to show up for everyone. It’s enabled by default, even on admin-controlled accounts.

title: This tool frees up Apple Intelligence storage on macOS, but think twice before using it
snippet: A new open-source tool is going viral over its promise to let users who aren’t interested in Apple Intelligence reclaim 12GB or more of storage on their Macs. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new open-source tool is going viral over its promise to let users who aren’t interested in Apple Intelligence reclaim 12GB or more of storage on their Macs. Here are the details.

’Turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models’

Like many companies adding AI tools and models across their platforms, Apple has faced criticism for features that take up storage space some users consider unnecessary.

While Apple Intelligence required up to 7GB of storage on macOS 26, that figure has increased significantly on macOS 27, with Apple now saying its latest models can require up to 14GB on newer Macs.

In response to this, indie developer Om Lahore published a project called RemoveMacAI on GitHub late last week, which promises to “turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models.”

As Lahore explains, his tool enables a configuration profile that applies Apple’s own restriction keys to turn off Apple Intelligence features, while also using the company’s asset service to remove downloaded models and prevent macOS from downloading them again.

He also explains exactly what the tool removes, which features it disables, and what users can expect after running it:

Features turned off: Siri (including “Hey Siri” and the menu bar icon), Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, the ChatGPT extension, summaries in Mail, Messages, Safari, Notes and notifications, Mail smart replies, inline text predictions, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode predictive code completion.

Models removed: the Apple Intelligence foundation models and the models for image generation and Genmoji, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode code completion.

And

What stops working? The features listed above, apps that use Apple’s on-device models (the Foundation Models framework and the Use Model action in Shortcuts), Visual Intelligence and natural-language editing in Calendar.

Lahore notes that dictation still works after running RemoveMacAI, as it “is a separate setting, and its speech models are not removed.”

Finally, he adds that the entire process can be reversed, with full details and instructions available here.

9to5Mac’s take

While part of the outcry over how much storage Apple Intelligence takes up on the Mac appears to be the same knee-jerk reaction against anything AI-related, there is a legitimate argument to be made for users with limited internal storage, particularly on 256GB Macs, where reclaiming 12GB or more can make a meaningful difference.

There is also a broader question of basic control over one’s own operating system, as users who have no interest in Apple Intelligence should arguably have a straightforward way to turn it off completely and recover the storage its models occupy, just as they can with other apps and certain optional parts of the system.

That said, there is no telling whether Apple will attempt to get the project removed from GitHub, or change the underlying mechanisms in macOS to make Apple Intelligence models harder to remove.

Likewise, there is no way to know how disabling or removing these components could affect macOS itself going forward, or even third-party apps that increasingly rely on Apple’s models to provide basic functionality.

While RemoveMacAI is open source and does not require disabling System Integrity Protection, it still relies on configuration profiles, restriction keys, and system services that Apple could change at any time.

	

That means a future macOS update could render parts of the tool ineffective, or potentially leave users dealing with unexpected behavior until the project is updated.

For now, anyone considering RemoveMacAI should understand that this is an unofficial third-party tool making system-level changes, and should be comfortable with the way it works.

To be completely clear, RemoveMacAI seems like a well-intentioned open-source project aimed at giving Mac users more autonomy and control over what runs on their computers and how their storage is used. It’s just impossible to know whether Apple will view it the same way.

title: Apple sets Q4 2026 earnings release for November 2
snippet: Apple will announce the results of its fiscal third quarter of 2026 on Monday, November 2. Here’s what to expect. more…
fullText:
Apple will announce the results of its fiscal third quarter of 2026 on Monday, November 2. Here’s what to expect.

Price increases likely to play major role

Apple confirmed today that it will report its Q4 2026 earnings on Monday, November 29.

Following the release of its quarterly results, the company will host a conference call at 2:00 p.m. PT / 5:00 p.m. ET, where John Ternus is expected to participate for the first time as Apple’s new CEO, alongside Apple CFO Kevan Parekh.

For its fiscal Q4 last year, Apple reported $102.47 billion in revenue, up 8%, and $27.47 billion in profit, a whopping 87% increase compared to a $14.7 billion profit in Q4 2024, as a result of a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge related to Apple’s long-running tax dispute in Ireland.

During last quarter’s earnings, Apple said it expected revenue for fiscal Q4 2026 to grow between 9% and 11% year over year, despite an expected 2.5 percentage-point foreign exchange headwind and significantly greater supply constraints affecting the iPhone, Mac, and iPad.

If that pans out, Apple’s revenue should come in between $111.69 billion and $113.74 billion. Apple also guided for a gross margin between 47% and 48%, down from 50.1% last quarter, although that figure included a roughly two-percentage-point benefit from tariff refunds.

In practical terms, Apple’s quarterly results will offer the first full-quarter look at the impact of the sweeping price increases it introduced across much of its hardware lineup in late June.

It is also worth noting that, since the reporting period for this fiscal quarter ended in late September, the results are unlikely to provide a meaningful indication of demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which also received price increases, as the new models only went on sale on September 18.

That said, Apple’s results will reveal how the company weathered another quarter of memory shortages and rising component costs, clearing the way for Ternus’s first full fiscal quarter as CEO to be reported in late January.

title: Android Auto might start requiring Android 11 or later soon, driver reports suggest
snippet: If you’re still holding onto an older Android phone as your daily driver, it might be losing its ability to get you where you need to be. Some users are starting to see notifications warning that their device will no longer be supported through Android Auto, suggesting the days of Android 10 are coming to a close. more…
fullText:
If you’re still holding onto an older Android phone as your daily driver, it might be losing its ability to get you where you need to be. Some users are starting to see notifications warning that their device will no longer be supported through Android Auto, suggesting the days of Android 10 are coming to a close.

Currently, Android Auto’s OS requirement is split into two tracks: wireless Auto support requires Android 11, while wired support requires just Android 9 Pie. A series of user reports over the weekend on Reddit (via Android Authority) suggest Google might be looking to unify those standards. The notification being delivered to drivers — most of whom appear to be running Android 10, not Android 9 Pie — simply states that Android Auto will “soon stop working on this phone,” without any additional context. Google has yet to update its current support page for Auto’s base-level requirements, but it’s not too difficult to read between the lines here.

Typically, I don’t think most users would see this change as a big surprise, even if cutting off support for certain phones always comes with controversy. In this case, though, it’s about as bad a time as you could pick for Google to be increasing device requirements. Some of the phones cited in these Reddit reports include Samsung’s Galaxy Note 9, Galaxy S9, and Xperia XZ2 Compact — all three of which offer experiences I’d argue are no longer available on the vast majority of modern Android devices. Add in the ever-increasing price of smartphones both new and not-so-new, and it feels a bit like a kick in the teeth to some drivers, no matter how old their hardware currently is.

If you’re an affected Android 9 Pie or Android 10 user and you need Android Auto support for your car, I would suggest starting to shop around for a replacement device running at least Android 11. While it’s a bad time to be in the market for any new gadget, there’s no obvious end to price hikes on the horizon, and picking up a phone now can save you some cash in the long run. We’ve reached out to Google for clarification on its Auto OS requirement plans and whether or not there’s a timeline for affected drivers to upgrade, and will update when we hear back.

fullText:
With the Amazon fall Prime Day event now underway, it is one of the best times of year to refresh your AirPods. While we are still awaiting holiday-worthy pricing on Apple’s latest AirPods 5 models, with AirPods Pro 3 down this low they might be a better buy for most folks anyway, and the 2026 AirPods Max 2 are now $120 off in all five colorways for those looking to get into the Apple over-ear experience. 

AirPods Pro 3 $179 (Reg. $249) 

AirPods Max 2 $429 (Reg. $549)

I’m personally quite impressed that Apple debuted its new entry-level AirPods 5 with active noise cancellation at the same $129 as the previous set without them. You’ll need to, however, jump up to the upgraded set at $149 to score the Wireless Charging Case, and that means you can land the much more advanced and high-end AirPods Pro for just $30 more right now – seems like a no-brainer to me. 

AirPods Pro 3 $179 (Reg. $249) 

Regularly $249, this is $70 off the list price and within just $10 of the lowest price we have ever seen on Amazon – a deal we have only tracked once since release. 

Down the road we will almost certainly see the new AirPods 5 starting at closer to $100 or less, but, if history and the previous generation are any indication, it might not be until well into 2027 before they plummet south of the $99 mark. And even once they do, the AirPods Pro 3 will still deliver 3x better noise cancellation, longer battery life, onboard heart rate sensors, all those Hearing Aid features, and, in my opinion, a much better fit. 

That’s a more than compelling argument to land the Pro 3 over the new series 5 sets, but if it’s the premium Apple over-ears you’re after, the fall Prime Day deal on Apple’s 2026 Max 2 are where it’s at. 

AirPods Max 2 $429 (Reg. $549)

Now sitting just $30 above the lowest price we have ever tracked on Amazon, you can land a set in any one of the five colorways at $120 off the list price. 

It is also worth pointing out that this is only the second time we have tracked them down this low since release earlier this year – only once have they ever sold for less. 

There are some other notable headphone deals from top brands like Sony and Bose (you’ll find those below), but there’s nothing quite like a Cupertino-designed personal listening experience if you ask me. If you’re not so convinced, you’ll find some admittedly solid options waiting below alongside a bevy of standout deals from across the Apple ecosystem.

title: Apple and AT&T Will Replace Your Brand New iPhone 18 Pro Max if It Can’t Connect
snippet: Update your phone now if you haven’t been affected, but the software fix won’t help for devices already broken by the problem.
fullText:
Barely three weeks after the iPhone 18 Pro Max arrived in customers’ hands, some AT&T customers are unable to make calls or get any cellular data — including dialing 911 in emergencies. Apple and AT&T rolled out a pair of fixes, but if you were bitten by this unusual bug, your shiny new iPhone is permanently broken and needs to be replaced, which Apple will do for free.

Last week, some iPhone 18 Pro Max owners on AT&T’s network reported no cellular access. MacRumors reported that AT&T sent a text message to iPhone 18 Pro Max owners, encouraging them to update to iOS 27.0.1 immediately. MacRumors estimates that thousands of customers have been affected.

On Friday, Apple said it’s issuing a separate carrier-settings patch to pair with the iOS 27.0.1 update. But the patch comes too late for certain owners of the new phone.

			

More from CNET

An Apple representative told CNET that the updates are intended to guard against this problem in the future and won’t fix the situation for iPhone 18 Pro Max owners who are already experiencing it. Apple will provide a new phone free of charge to those owners. Affected customers should contact Apple Support or AT&T.

In Reddit threads about the issue, some owners confirmed that the 27.0.1 update by itself did not fix the problem, nor did upgrading to the public beta of iOS 27.2.

Only the iPhone 18 Pro Max is affected

So far, the issue seems limited to iPhone 18 Pro Max models on AT&T’s network. I reached out to contacts at T-Mobile and Verizon, and both report they’re not seeing similar reports on their networks. I haven’t experienced the issue on an iPhone 18 Pro that runs on AT&T’s network, which isn’t surprising given that this particular problem affects iPhone 18 Pro Max units, not iPhone 18 Pro phones. A CNET colleague’s iPhone 18 Pro Max on Google Fi (which uses T-Mobile’s network) is not experiencing the issue. I’ve not been able to discern if customers of cellular providers that use AT&T’s network, such as Cricket or US Mobile, have been affected.

It’s unclear whether the lack of connectivity is related to the phone’s hardware. While the standard iPhone 18 Pro is equipped with Apple’s C2 modem, the iPhone 18 Pro Max in the US is the only model with Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80 modem, as shown in this teardown of the phone by iFixIt. Qualcomm has been Apple’s modem provider for years, but Apple has worked to move away from relying on the third party for the essential phone component. That relationship is due to expire this year.

According to a TechInsights iPhone 18 Pro Max teardown, the X80 modem is also used in the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max, but a new millimeter-wave antenna has been added to the 18 Pro Max. Millimeter-wave offers much faster data speeds in areas where the technology is installed, but it can have a shorter range and be reduced by obstacles. Apple’s C2 modem also includes a millimeter-wave antenna.

Qualcomm declined to comment, and a representative directed me to contact Apple for more information.

Apple and AT&T rolled out a pair of fixes, but if you were bitten by this unusual bug, your shiny new iPhone is permanently broken and needs to be replaced, which Apple will do for free.

Last week, some iPhone 18 Pro Max owners on AT&T’s network reported no cellular access. MacRumors reported that AT&T sent a text message to iPhone 18 Pro Max owners, encouraging them to update to iOS 27.0.1 immediately. MacRumors estimates that thousands of customers have been affected.

title: Formula 1 on Apple TV is getting Dolby Atmos, starting this month
snippet: Beginning with the U.S. Grand Prix weekend on Friday, October 23, Apple TV will offer Formula 1 coverage in Dolby Atmos on supported devices. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Beginning with the U.S. Grand Prix weekend on Friday, October 23, Apple TV will offer Formula 1 coverage in Dolby Atmos on supported devices. Here are the details.

’Bringing exceptional picture and sound together to capture the full intensity of the sport’

Apple and Dolby Laboratories announced a new partnership to bring Dolby Atmos to Apple TV’s live Formula 1 coverage, starting with the U.S. Grand Prix weekend, which begins October 23 in Austin, Texas.

Apple says Dolby Atmos will join “Dolby Vision to deliver an even more immersive viewing experience,” putting “fans at the heart of the action, surrounding them with the energy, drama, and emotion of Formula 1.”

From team radio communications and race commentary to the roar of the engines, on-track battles, and the intensity of the pit lane, Dolby Atmos brings the unmistakable sounds that define the sport to life.

Here’s Oliver Schusser, Vice President of Apple Music and International Content at Apple, on the announcement:

“We’re always looking for new ways to make Formula 1 on Apple TV even better for fans. […] The sound of Formula 1 is such an important part of what makes the sport so exciting, and with Dolby Atmos joining Dolby Vision, fans can experience the energy and intensity of every Grand Prix in a whole new way. It’s another example of how we’re continuing to innovate across the viewing experience to bring fans closer to the action.”

It’s worth noting that Apple TV’s streaming rights for Formula 1 still include only the U.S., but don’t require an extra subscription on top of the Apple TV subscription.

Apple recently made the Bahrain Grand Prix available to stream for free in the U.S., and has also partnered with Netflix to bring Formula 1: Drive to Survive Season 8 to Apple TV in the U.S. As part of the same collaboration, the 2026 Canadian Grand Prix was streamed live on both Apple TV and Netflix in the U.S.

Apple secured the U.S. streaming rights to Formula 1 in 2025 as part of a five-year deal beginning with the 2026 season, and has previously indicated it wants to expand its F1 coverage into additional markets.

Apple’s broader relationship with Formula 1 also includes “F1: The Movie,” which won the Academy Award for Best Sound earlier this year and remains Apple’s biggest theatrical success to date.

Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month or as part of the Apple One bundle. It features hit TV shows and movies like Ted Lasso, Severance, The Studio, The Morning Show, Shrinking, and Silo.

title: YouTube says Shorts recommendations won’t surface unoriginal content
snippet: YouTube says it wants to ‘focus on originality’ in a push to surface better Shorts recommendations for users. more…
fullText:
YouTube says it wants to ‘focus on originality’ in a push to surface better Shorts recommendations for users.

Shorts is built on quick and attention-grabbing content, which makes cutting portions of long-form videos one of the easiest ways to put out quick videos with high view potential. Of course, that also means channels can just as easily take content from other established creators and stamp out short-form videos from it.

YouTube says it’s adjusted its Shorts recommendations so users will see less unoriginal content. Users who upload content that blatantly steals video from another channel will not get the same reach as they did before the change, according to what YouTube laid out in its release.

To improve the Shorts experience for everyone, we’re updating our recommendation systems to further prioritize original content and reduce the reach of content re-uploaded from other creators without adding anything of your own.

There’s a small amount of room for interpretation. YouTube’s language seems to imply that Shorts that contain no changes form another’s work would be affected, but no clear line in the sand has been drawn out.

	

Remember, YouTube announced it was testing a new feature that would let users reimagine other channels’ videos using AI, which was released in March. Whether those videos will still be surfaced in the recommendations system is unclear.

The change should mean users will see a focus on original content, and creators that upload original Shorts will likely be rewarded. YouTube hasn’t detailed a rollout date for this change, but it sounds like it may be live already.

title: A New Study Puts the Heat on Gas Stoves for Commercial Kitchen Air Pollution
snippet: The gas versus electric stove debate continues.
fullText:
Following a July study that found switching from a household gas stove to an electric one can improve asthma symptoms, a new peer-reviewed study published on Tuesday concluded that workers in restaurant kitchens using gas and propane appliances are exposed to air pollution and heat levels that exceed health guidelines.

The National Restaurant Association reports that over 15.7 million Americans work in the food service industry. 

Published in the scientific journal Environmental Research Letters, and in collaboration with chef Christopher Galarza, the study was conducted by researchers from the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability, the New York University Grossman School of Medicine and PSE Healthy Energy, an independent scientific research institute specializing in bringing science to energy policy. 

			

More from CNET

According to a press release, this is the first US study to compare air quality and heat levels in restaurant kitchens that use gas appliances with those that use all-electric appliances under real-world working conditions. The study is part of PSE Healthy Energy’s Methane and Health Initiative, which uncovers air quality and health risks associated with methane sources to protect public health and the climate. 

Researchers measured air temperature and air pollutants produced by gas stoves: methane, nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and benzene. Measurements were taken in five employee work areas, both during service and overnight, in 21 gas kitchens, three propane kitchens and three all-electric kitchens in California, New York and Pennsylvania. 

“Everyone likely has a favorite restaurant or fast food chain, but most people probably haven’t thought about the equipment being used and how that affects what the staff is experiencing in the kitchen area,” Drew Michanowicz, principal scientist at PSE Healthy Energy, told CNET in an email.

Air pollution findings

When kitchens are not properly ventilated, pollutants can build up and cause harmful health effects, though this depends on individual sensitivity and exposure level. 

During the study, it was discovered that in kitchens with gas or propane appliances, at least one health guideline for pollutant exposure was exceeded during cooking hours. 

About 70% of gas kitchens in the study surpassed the US Environmental Protection Agency’s 1-hour outdoor air standard for nitrogen dioxide. The outdoor standard was used because there is no comparable indoor standard in the US. 

In kitchens with gas or propane appliances, about 170 cumulative hours (about four full work weeks) were recorded in which nitrogen dioxide concentrations exceeded the World Health Organization’s hour-averaged exposure recommendation. This recommendation is roughly equal to the EPA’s outdoor standard, and both apply to the general population.

One kitchen’s 15-minute average nitrogen dioxide level exceeded the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health’s recommended short-term workplace exposure limit.

Nitrogen dioxide can cause reduced lung function, increased asthma attacks, increased airway inflammation, and worsened cough and wheezing. This gaseous air pollutant has even been tied to causing asthma in children. 

The study also found that carbon monoxide and benzene concentrations exceeded California’s 1-hour exposure guidelines in three and five gas kitchens, respectively. Carbon monoxide poisoning symptoms can range from a headache and dizziness to passing out and death. Benzene, on the other hand, is a carcinogen that has been linked to a higher risk of leukemia and other blood cell cancers.

By comparison, no all-electric kitchen exceeded pollution-exposure health guidelines during cooking hours. 

“This study emphasizes that the concentrations of pollutants in commercial kitchens with gas-fired appliances can reach levels even higher than what we’ve previously observed in homes with gas stoves,” Yannai Kashtan, an air quality scientist at PSE Healthy Energy, told CNET in an email.

Those actually working in the kitchen aren’t the only ones who could be affected.Rhenizara S/Getty Images

Overnight levels matter too

Even outside cooking hours, exposure remains a concern, according to new evidence from the study. 

When gas appliance pilot lights remain lit, and ventilation is turned off, cleaning crews and staff arriving early risk exposure to pollutants. About 71% of the gas kitchens with overnight monitoring recorded higher levels of nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, methane and benzene overnight than during service hours.

Aside from contributing to climate change, high concentrations of methane can displace oxygen in the air, causing fatigue, rapid breathing, vomiting, collapse, convulsions, organ damage and death. 

When you consider that commercial gas appliances are also used in hospitals, schools and other buildings, the health concerns extend beyond restaurant kitchens.  

None of the all-electric kitchens exceeded pollutant guidelines overnight. 

Temperature findings

When it came to heat health guidelines, about 68% of gas kitchens with temperature data exceeded 90 degrees Fahrenheit, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration’s proposed high-heat threshold.

Even when temperatures outside were below 75 degrees Fahrenheit, 10 of 13 gas kitchens exceeded 90 degrees Fahrenheit, meaning that high heat in commercial kitchens isn’t directly tied to the weather. 

When a temperature monitor was attached to a chef’s shoulder during a 5-hour cooking session, the average temperature was 92 degrees Fahrenheit, with a maximum of 106 degrees Fahrenheit.

Guidelines differ between the general population and the workplace, which could put workers’ health at risk.andresr/Getty Images

A guideline gap in kitchen worker protection

The study compared its findings with both EPA and WHO guidelines for the general population, which prioritize health protection, and with NIOSH and OSHA guidelines, which are occupational. Researchers found fewer instances of kitchens exceeding workplace thresholds. 

“Compared to benchmarks for the general population, occupational thresholds are higher because they serve a different purpose by also accounting for industry cost and technical feasibility,” Kashtan said. “If work environments are exceeding health-based thresholds but are compliant with the occupational limits that govern enforcement, this points to a gap in health protection for commercial kitchen workers.”

The study’s limitations

Due to the scarcity of all-electric commercial kitchens, only three were used in this study. However, the researchers stated in the study that their findings remain consistent with prior research on nitrogen dioxide concentrations from gas versus electric appliances. 

As about 80% of end-use energy in US commercial cooking is gas, the small number of all-electric kitchens used in the study also reflects the current restaurant industry. 

Only restaurant kitchens in three states were used, so this may not reflect the broader US. Participation was voluntary and partly facilitated through professional partnerships, so selection bias may have been introduced, especially given that kitchens willing to participate likely had better working conditions. 

While sampling locations were chosen to account for different worker roles in the kitchen, pollutant measurements may differ from actual exposure due to a worker’s movement, health, posture and proximity to emission sources. These locations also weren’t monitored continuously; instead, they were sampled for 5 to 12 minutes per cycle. 

Particulate matter and WBGT, which measures occupational heat stress, were not measured. 

Ensure that your range hood is maintained and turned on when cooking.SBenitez/Getty Images

Restaurant recommendations

Based on this study, Michanowicz has three recommendations for worker protections in commercial kitchens that use gas appliances. 

First, it’s important to ensure that ventilation systems are properly maintained, as these are usually the first line of defense against pollution and excess heat. However, even with these systems in place, restaurant workers who work directly over a cooking surface can still be exposed to pollution and heat before they reach the ventilation system. 

While converting a commercial kitchen from gas to electric can be challenging and costly, focusing on electrifying gas ranges and fryers first can yield the greatest benefits for indoor air quality. 

“There are also additional benefits that chefs we worked with have mentioned, such as higher worker productivity due to more comfortable kitchen temperatures, reduced cleaning times and reduced burn and explosion risks,” Michanowicz said.

Lastly, for workers in commercial kitchens during off-hours, including cleaning crews, when pilot lights are still on, ventilation systems should be turned on. This applies to workers who arrive early in the morning, as pollution will have built up overnight. 

Gas stove household advice

The recommendations for those with gas stoves at home aren’t dissimilar. 

“The best way to reduce gas combustion pollution is to eliminate the source – the gas flame – and to get an electric radiant or induction stove,” said Kashtan. 

However, if that’s not possible due to cost or because one is a renter, cooking can still be partially electrified with air fryers, electric kettles, rice cookers and portable induction hobs. 

And when you do use your gas stove, always make sure your range hood is on, and consider putting an air purifier in your kitchen.

title: Apple’s new ‘homeOS’ will launch this month, here’s what’s coming
snippet: Apple reportedly plans to launch new Home products on October 13 alongside an all-new operating system rumored to be called ‘homeOS.’ Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple reportedly plans to launch new Home products on October 13 alongside an all-new operating system rumored to be called ‘homeOS.’ Here are the details.

homeOS will run on new ‘HomePad’ product, featuring mix of other Apple OS designs

Apple’s highly anticipated ‘HomePad’ smart home hub is reportedly being unveiled on October 13. And per Mark Gurman, it will run on a brand new operating system that’s rumored to be called ‘homeOS.’

A recent Bloomberg report offers a lot of details on what to expect from homeOS. It reportedly features a blend of other Apple OS designs, including:

iPhone-style widgets

iPad-like app designs

Apple Watch-style icons for its Home Screen 

The default UI, per Gurman, “is built heavily around photo slideshows and clock displays, similar to the new StandBy Mode on the upcoming iPhone Duo” and users can “swipe up from the clock screen or photos to open the app launcher.”

We’ve seen multiple leaks this past week around this Photo Face in homeOS, as seen below.

Siri AI is the central input method, but Apple apps and a Home Screen will also be available via touch

Siri AI will be central to homeOS interactions. Per Gurman on his new podcast:

The new operating system is basically, what would an OS look like if Siri AI had an OS? If Siri AI was not just an app on the phone, if it wasn’t just an interface on the phone. What if it was an operating system?…It’s all about this concept of personal search and personal context, being able to ask for songs, podcasts, notes, calendar items, photos that are bespoke to you.

Voice won’t be the only interaction method though. Apple apps and a Home Screen will be part of homeOS too. Siri AI can be used to control these apps, but touch input will be supported too.

Built-in homeOS apps will include Music, Podcasts, Photos, Weather, FaceTime, Notes, Calendar, Messages, Reminders, and more. No App Store is expected to be available, but third-party widgets can be brought over from your iPhone.

Like on the current HomePod though, the idea is that most of the time, your interactions with homeOS happen via Siri.

title: Google Wallet rolling out stacked card list redesign on Android
snippet: After updating the bottom half of the homepage earlier this year, Google Wallet for Android is rolling out a stacked list redesign for accessing credit and debit cards. more…
fullText:
After updating the bottom half of the homepage earlier this year, Google Wallet for Android is rolling out a stacked list redesign for accessing credit and debit cards.

The previous design made use of a carousel to show your stored payment methods. This design showed just a sliver of the next and previous cards at the edges. Google allowed you to reorder cards and set a default one.

	

With this stacked redesign, the homepage shows one full card preview and the sliver of a second at the top. To expand, you tap or swipe down to enter the fullscreen layout that shows most of each card. “Manage payment methods” at the bottom lets you arrange the order and set the default.

You select a card to tap-to-pay. To see card details and transaction history, there’s a new settings gear icon in the top-right corner. This adds an extra step compared to the previous approach.

	

This approach is nice for one-handed use, especially if your most used cards are placed at the bottom. There are no other changes to the Google Wallet homepage.

This redesign started appearing in September and is now seeing broader availability. It’s rolling out via a server-side update and appeared on several devices we checked today.

title: Googlebooks can’t install the Slack web app on day one
snippet: Googlebook is now on sale and shipping to customers and, on day one at least, they can’t install the Slack web app. more…
fullText:
Googlebook is now on sale and shipping to customers and, on day one at least, they can’t install the Slack web app. 

Googlebook as a platform relies on two main forms of apps. The first is native Android apps, as Googlebook OS is, at its core, Android. That’s what you’ll use for many experiences including Gemini, Google Photos, music apps, and more. Others, like Gmail and YouTube, instead rely on progressive web apps. That term might sound familiar if you’re a long-time Chromebook user, as Chromebooks bet pretty heavily on progressive web apps (PWAs).

That history aside, Googlebooks directly tell their users to use Slack through the web app. The Play Store puts up a banner saying that Slack is “better on the website” when you try to download the Android app. 

That’s correct, frankly, as Slack’s Android app has terrible support for anything besides a standard smartphone. 

	

But the Slack web app cannot be installed on a Googlebook at this time.

	

Trying to install the Slack web app as a PWA on Googlebook results in an error message saying that “this app cannot be installed.” You can still create a shortcut that opens as a Chrome tab, but it won’t open in a window. 

Other PWAs we’ve tested including Photopea, Squoosh, SnapDrop, and others seem to be working fine. It’s unclear why Slack in particular is broken, but it’s hard to imagine it’s the only PWA not working on Googlebook on day one. More importantly, Slack is a mainstay in the modern workspace, so lacking any form of desktop-level Slack support on day one is sure to leave a poor impression on early Googlebook adopters.

Update: Google, in a statement, says that Slack is not a “compliant” PWA but that Googlebook will add support for manual installation soon.

Installing PWAs is fully supported on Googlebooks. But, the Slack web app isn’t a compliant PWA. Chrome on ChromeOS allows manual installation even though it’s not a PWA. This capability will also be coming to Chrome on Googlebooks soon.

by  Emma Roth

Oct 7, 2026, 2:40 PM UTC

Photo by Angela Weiss/AFP via Getty Images

Emma Roth

 

is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Google DeepMind, Meta, and AI drug discovery startup Isomorphic Labs are jointly investing $300 million into Biohub, the nonprofit biomedical research organization founded by Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan, as reported by Reuters. The funding is part of a $1.8 billion initiative to build AI datasets that could allow researchers to “ask, predict, and answer biological questions digitally,” helping find new ways to prevent and manage diseases.

Founded in 2016, Biohub aims to combat diseases through the creation of a “virtual cell” that researchers can use to carry out simulations. To support this effort, the US Department of Energy will invest more than $500 million over the next five years, while the National Institutes of Health will contribute datasets, repositories, and knowledge bases stemming from previous federal investment totalling over $500 million.

“An accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery by enabling scientists to perform experiments digitally,” Alex Rives, Biohub’s head of science, says in the press release. “The creation of a virtual cell is one of the most important challenges for the next era of science. It will require coordinated data generation efforts at a national and international scale, which is why these partners are coming together.”

title: iFixit tears down Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, finds mixed repairability results
snippet: Concluding iFixit’s teardown sequence for Apple’s September launches, iFixit today published the teardown of the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Here’s what they found. more…
fullText:
Concluding iFixit’s teardown sequence for Apple’s September launches, iFixit today published the teardown of the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Here’s what they found.

iFixit tears down Apple Watch Ultra 4

After applying heat to the new Apple Watch Ultra 4’s screen, iFixit’s Shahram Mokhtari uses the company’s new metal pick to pry the screen open, exposing the battery and the Taptic Engine.

He notes that replacing the 2.444 Wh battery (versus 2.313 Wh in the Ultra 3) still requires removing the screen, which remains a significant repairability drawback. The four screws on the bottom of the case provide access only to the sensor assembly on the underside of the back cover and the S11 chip on the case itself.

Once the screen is unglued, though, removing the battery and disconnecting the display’s press connector seems straightforward enough, provided that the initial step was done carefully enough to avoid slicing through any of the flex cables underneath.

That said, with no significant improvements in repairability, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 scored 4/10 on iFixit’s repairability scale, the same as its predecessor.

iFixit tears down Apple Watch Series 12

iFixit’s teardown of the new Apple Watch Series 12 revealed a slight repairability improvement, with Apple adding stretch-release adhesive and a pull tab that make the 1.461 Wh battery (versus 1.403 Wh in the 46mm Series 11) easier to remove.

Still, as with the Apple Watch Ultra 4, the Series 12 also requires prying off the glued display to get inside, which remains the biggest obstacle to repairs. Mokhtari noted that the tolerances around the Series 12’s display are even tighter than on the Ultra 4, requiring enough force to make him concerned about potentially damaging the screen.

Mokhtari also noted that Apple replaced the ZIF connector and tape used for the display on previous models with a simpler press connector.

The tradeoff is that replacing the screen now also requires removing and replacing the battery, “which, if you’ve come this far, why wouldn’t you?” he adds.

All in all, the modest repairability improvements were enough for iFixit to give the Series 12 a 4/10 repairability score, a 1-point bump from the last base-model Apple Watch it scored.

For comparison, iFixit gave Google’s Pixel Watch 5 a 9/10 repairability score, noting that its display can be removed with just two Torx screws and a gasket, while its battery can also be removed without dealing with adhesive.
